definition_zh: 抑制；阻止；约束；禁止；使（生物或化学反应）受抑制
definition_en: to hold something back, slow it down or keep it from acting freely
core_image: 一只手紧紧按住正在弹开的阀门手柄，压力表指针停在原位不再上冲
scene: 实验台上，学生往培养皿里滴入一滴药剂，菌落的扩散立刻停在划好的圈内。A single dose can inhibit the growth of the bacteria for hours.
sceneCN: 这里指用药剂阻止细菌继续生长（第 1 个义项：抑制生物或化学过程）；句意为一次给药就能让这些细菌的生长停止数小时。

derivatives.zh: 由动词加表示「行为、状态」的名词尾构成，义为「抑制；拘谨」
由动词加表示「施动者」的名词尾构成，义为「抑制剂；抑制物」
由动词加表示「起……作用的」形容词尾构成，义为「抑制性的」
由动词加已然词尾构成，义为「受抑制的；拘谨的」
由动词加表示「倾向于」的形容词尾构成，义为「有抑制作用的」
由表示「不」的前缀加已然形容词构成，义为「不受约束的；放纵的」

senses.title: Slow a living or chemical process
senses.definition: to reduce the rate or extent of a biological or chemical process
senses.definitionCN: 降低生物或化学过程的速度或程度
senses.example: Cold temperatures inhibit the growth of most moulds.
senses.exampleCN: 低温会抑制大多数霉菌的生长。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to hold in, and a process that is held in simply runs slower.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词本义是「按住、拦住」，被按住的过程自然就跑得慢了。

senses.title: Hold a person back
senses.definition: to make a person less willing or less able to act freely
senses.definitionCN: 使人不愿或不能自由行动
senses.example: Fear of criticism inhibited her from speaking at the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 对批评的畏惧使她不敢在会上发言。
senses.why: The same holding image applies to a person: something inside keeps the action from coming out.
senses.whyCN: 同一个「按住」的意象也用在人身上：心里有东西把行动压了回去。

senses.title: Block an enzyme or reaction
senses.definition: to interfere with a molecule or reaction so that it cannot proceed normally
senses.definitionCN: 干扰分子或反应，使其无法正常进行
senses.example: The drug inhibits an enzyme that the virus needs to copy itself.
senses.exampleCN: 这种药抑制病毒复制自身所需的一种酶。
senses.why: Biochemistry borrowed the word for anything that stops a molecular step, since stopping is a form of holding back.
senses.whyCN: 生物化学借这个词指任何阻断分子步骤的东西，因为阻断就是一种按住。

senses.title: Forbid by authority
senses.definition: to forbid something officially, especially by a church or a legal authority
senses.definitionCN: 由教会或法律权威正式禁止某事
senses.example: The old rule inhibited the sale of land to outsiders.
senses.exampleCN: 旧规定禁止把土地卖给外来者。
senses.why: Church law used the word for a formal ban, and the meaning of a public prohibition grew from that usage.
senses.whyCN: 教会法用这个词表示正式禁令，公开禁止的含义就是从这种用法长出来的。

senses.title: Dampen growth or development
senses.definition: to keep an economy, industry or activity from expanding as it otherwise would
senses.definitionCN: 使经济、行业或活动无法按原本的速度扩张
senses.example: High taxes may inhibit small firms from hiring.
senses.exampleCN: 高税收可能抑制小企业招人。
senses.why: An expanding thing is imagined as a force pushing outward, and inhibiting is the hand that pushes back.
senses.whyCN: 扩张的事物被想象成向外推的力量，而抑制就是把它推回去的那只手。

senses.title: Suppress a nerve signal
senses.definition: to reduce or block the transmission of a signal along a nerve or circuit
senses.definitionCN: 减弱或阻断沿神经或电路传递的信号
senses.example: This pathway inhibits the nerve that carries the pain signal.
senses.exampleCN: 这条通路会抑制传递疼痛信号的神经。
senses.why: In physiology the word names the braking side of the nervous system, the part that holds a signal down.
senses.whyCN: 在生理学里，这个词指神经系统中「刹车」的那一侧，也就是把信号按住的部分。

senses.title: Restrain an impulse or emotion
senses.definition: to keep an impulse or feeling from being expressed openly
senses.definitionCN: 使冲动或情绪不被公开表达出来
senses.example: He had learned to inhibit his anger in front of clients.
senses.exampleCN: 他学会了在客户面前克制自己的怒气。
senses.why: Social training is described as a restraint placed on feeling, which is the literal sense applied inward.
senses.whyCN: 社会训练被描述为对情绪施加的约束，这就是字面义转向内心的用法。

senses.title: Hold back investment or activity
senses.definition: to make investors or buyers unwilling to spend, so that activity falls
senses.definitionCN: 使投资者或买家不愿支出，从而使活动减少
senses.example: Uncertainty about the rules inhibited investment for two years.
senses.exampleCN: 规则不明朗抑制了投资长达两年。
senses.why: Money that is held back does not circulate, and the word covers that economic hesitation as well.
senses.whyCN: 被按住的钱不流通，这个词也覆盖这种经济上的迟疑。

intro.en: Inhibit comes from Latin inhibere, to hold in or keep back, built from in-, into, and habere, to hold. English first used it for official prohibitions, then for any restraining force, including chemical and neural ones.
intro.cn: 这个词来自拉丁语 inhibere「按住、拦住」，由表示「向内」的前缀与表示「持有、握住」的词根构成。英语最初用它表示官方禁止，后来扩展到任何起约束作用的力量，包括化学与神经层面的抑制。

items.en: Habere meant to have or hold, and it stands behind a large family of English words about possession and restraint.
items.cn: 这个词根意为「有、握住」，英语中一大批表示持有与约束的词都出自它。

items.en: The prefix in- added the idea of direction inward, so the verb pictured a force holding something inside its own limits.
items.cn: 前缀给它加上「向内」的方向，于是这个动词画出的是把某物按在其限度之内的力。

items.en: The action noun named a keeping back or a prohibition, and it passed into English as inhibition.
items.cn: 动作名词表示「按住、禁止」，进入英语后成为「抑制」这一名词。

items.en: English took the verb through French and used it first for forbidding a person from acting; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语经法语引入这个动词，最初用于禁止某人行动；确切的最早年代不确定。

items.en: A bishop could inhibit a cleric from exercising office, and the word carried that official weight for centuries.
items.cn: 主教可以禁止教士行使职务，这个词带着这种官方分量用了好几个世纪。

items.en: Physiology and chemistry adopted the word for any agent that slows a process, and that sense now dominates.
items.cn: 生理学与化学采用这个词指任何使过程变慢的因素，这一义项如今占主导。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin root or merely looks similar; the second group gathers verbs of restraining and forbidding.
note.cn: 第一组或共享拉丁词根，或只是形近；第二组收集表示约束与禁止的动词。

entries.definition: The noun for the act of restraining, and also for shyness that holds a person back.
entries.definitionCN: 指抑制行为，也指使人退缩的拘谨。

entries.definition: A substance or device that slows or blocks a process.
entries.definitionCN: 指使过程变慢或被阻断的物质或装置。

entries.definition: Held back from free expression; reserved in manner.
entries.definitionCN: 指表达受压抑、举止拘谨的。

entries.definition: Free from restraint and showing feelings openly.
entries.definitionCN: 指不受约束、坦然表露情感的。

entries.definition: To show something publicly; it shares the hold root but the prefix points outward.
entries.definitionCN: 指公开展示；与抑制共享「握住」词根，但前缀指向外。

entries.definition: To live in a place; it looks close but belongs to the root for dwelling, not for holding.
entries.definitionCN: 指居住于某地；形近但属于「居住」词根，与「握住」无关。

entries.definition: To keep someone or something under control, often by physical or moral force.
entries.definitionCN: 指以体力或道德力量把某人某事控制住。

entries.definition: To stop something by force, or to keep a feeling from showing.
entries.definitionCN: 指以强力制止，或压住情绪不使其外露。

entries.definition: To make an action slower or harder without stopping it completely.
entries.definitionCN: 指使行动变慢或变难，但不完全停止。

entries.definition: To forbid something by law or rule.
entries.definitionCN: 指依法律或规章禁止某事。

entries.definition: To keep something within limits, especially spending or growth.
entries.definitionCN: 指把开支或增长等控制在限度内。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the holding image, the real word family and the real scientific phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用「按住」的意象、真实的同族词与真实的科学搭配。

normal.en: In- means in and habere means hold, so inhibit is literally to hold in.
normal.cn: 前缀意为「向内」，词根意为「握住」，所以这个词字面上就是「往里按住」。

normal.en: An inhibitor is the thing that does the holding, and inhibition is the holding itself.
normal.cn: 抑制剂是执行按住的东西，抑制则是按住这个动作本身。

normal.en: A hand on a valve is the clearest picture: the flow is still there, only stopped.
normal.cn: 一只手按在阀门上是最清楚的画面：流仍在，只是被停住了。

normal.en: The word appears in enzyme inhibitor and immune inhibition, two fixed scientific phrases.
normal.cn: 这个词出现在「酶抑制剂」与「免疫抑制」两个固定的科学说法里。

normal.en: Inhibited behaviour is a person whose impulse has been held down before it reached the surface.
normal.cn: 拘谨的行为，就是冲动在浮出表面之前被按住了的人。

abstract.en: Restraint is not destruction: what is inhibited still exists, which is why a drug can stop a virus without killing it.
abstract.cn: 约束不等于毁灭：被抑制的东西仍然存在，所以药物能阻止病毒却不杀死它。

abstract.en: Every brake is a small inhibition, and a society is full of brakes that nobody calls by this name.
abstract.cn: 每一副刹车都是一次小小的抑制，社会里到处是没人用这个词称呼的刹车。

abstract.en: The word teaches that stopping and holding are the same gesture seen from two sides.
abstract.cn: 这个词说明，停止与按住是同一个手势的两面。

examples.en: Dry weather can inhibit the germination of these seeds.
examples.cn: 干燥天气会抑制这些种子发芽。

examples.en: The regulation was designed to inhibit speculation in the housing market.
examples.cn: 这项规定旨在抑制住房市场中的投机。

examples.en: A low dose inhibits the enzyme without damaging the surrounding tissue.
examples.cn: 低剂量会抑制这种酶，又不损伤周围组织。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「因希比特」——把「因」由都按在「希」望的「比特」上：按住不让动，就是抑制、阻止

root: 拉丁语 inhibere「按住、拦住」← in-「向内」+ habere「持有、握住」；同根词有 exhibit「展出」（向外持）、inhibition「抑制」。英语十五世纪经法语引入，先用于教会与法律上的禁止，十九世纪后扩展到生理与化学的抑制。最早年代为约数。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses run from the laboratory to the courtroom: slowing a living process, holding a person back, blocking an enzyme, forbidding by authority, dampening growth, suppressing a nerve signal, restraining an impulse, and holding back investment.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从实验室延伸到法庭：减慢生命过程、约束人的行动、阻断酶、以权力禁止、抑制增长、抑制神经信号、克制冲动、抑制投资。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a firm hand presses a valve shut, and the pressure that was rising stops where it stands.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手把阀门牢牢按住，原本上升的压力停在原处。

branches.en: THE SLOWED PROCESS: growth and expansion that are held to a lower rate.
branches.cn: 被减慢的过程：增长与扩张被压到更低的速率。

branches.en: THE RESTRAINED PERSON: action and feeling kept from coming out.
branches.cn: 被约束的人：行动与情绪被压住不外露。

branches.en: THE BLOCKED SIGNAL: an enzyme step or a nerve impulse that cannot pass.
branches.cn: 被阻断的信号：酶的步骤或神经冲动无法通过。

branches.en: THE OFFICIAL BAN: a rule that forbids an act by authority.
branches.cn: 官方禁令：由权威以规则禁止某种行为。

branches.en: THE HELD-BACK MONEY: spending that waits instead of circulating.
branches.cn: 被按住的钱：支出停住而不流通。

intro.en: Inhibit is a Latin verb whose prefix and root still work separately in English words.
intro.cn: 这是一个拉丁动词，它的前缀与词根在英语其他词里仍然各自起作用。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies habere and inhibere; the family also includes the prefixed form exhibere, to hold out or show.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了「持有」与「按住」两个词；同族还包括加外向前缀的「伸出、展示」。

items.example: It turns holding into holding in.
items.exampleCN: 它把「持」变成「向内按住」。

items.example: The root of many English words about possession.
items.exampleCN: 英语中许多表示拥有的词的词根。

items.example: The direct source of the English verb.
items.exampleCN: 英语动词的直接来源。

items.example: It became the English noun inhibition.
items.exampleCN: 它成为英语名词「抑制」。

items.example: It forms inhibition from the verb.
items.exampleCN: 它把动词构成「抑制」这一名词。

items.example: It forms inhibitor for the substance.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示物质的名词「抑制剂」。

items.example: It forms inhibitory for a kind of effect.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示作用性质的形容词。

items.example: It forms the adjective inhibited.
items.exampleCN: 它构成形容词「受抑制的」。

items.example: It forms uninhibited, the opposite.
items.exampleCN: 它构成反义词「不受约束的」。

items.example: It made exhibere, to hold out and show, the source of exhibit.
items.exampleCN: 它与同一词根构成「向外持」，即「展出」的来源。

derivatives.zh: 由动词加表示动作的名词尾构成，义为「抑制；拘谨」
加施动者名词尾，义为「抑制剂」
加功能性形容词尾，义为「抑制性的」
加已然词尾，义为「受抑制的；拘谨的」
加否定前缀，义为「不受约束的」

definition_zh: 理论框架；指导研究并解释现象的一整套理论、假设与概念结构
definition_en: an organized set of theories, assumptions and concepts that guides a study and explains what it observes
core_image: 一张摊开的大图纸上，几根主梁先立稳，再把各块薄板搭到梁上，整间屋子的受力关系一眼可见
scene: 开题报告写到研究思路一节，导师要求学生先把所依据的理论体系搭清楚，再谈具体方法。Every thesis needs a theoretical framework before the methods are chosen.
sceneCN: 这里指研究开始前先搭好的理论体系（第 1 个义项：指导研究的理论结构）；句意为每篇论文在选定方法之前都需要一个理论框架。

collocations.zh: 以某一理论框架为基础

derivatives.zh: 由希腊语「观看、沉思」而来的名词，义为「理论；学说」
由「理论」加表示「属于……的」形容词尾构成，义为「理论的」
在形容词后加副词尾，义为「在理论上」
加表示「从事者」的名词尾，义为「理论家」
加表示「使……化」的动词尾，义为「建立理论」

senses.title: The overall theory that guides a study
senses.titleCN: 统领整项研究的理论结构
senses.definition: the organized body of theory that defines what a study looks at and how it interprets results
senses.definitionCN: 界定研究看什么、如何解释结果的成体系理论
senses.example: The theoretical framework draws on two models of learning.
senses.exampleCN: 这个理论框架借用了两种学习模型。
senses.why: A framework is a load-bearing structure, and theory supplies the beams that hold a study upright.
senses.whyCN: 框架是承重结构，而理论提供把研究撑起来的梁。

senses.title: A set of assumptions and definitions
senses.definition: the assumptions and defined terms that a study accepts before any data are collected
senses.definitionCN: 研究在收集数据之前就已接受的一组假设与界定好的术语
senses.example: Her theoretical framework treats motivation as a stable trait.
senses.exampleCN: 她的理论框架把动机视为一种稳定特质。
senses.why: Every framework begins by fixing what its words mean, just as a building begins with fixed dimensions.
senses.whyCN: 每个框架都先固定词的含义，正如建筑先固定尺寸。

senses.title: An explanatory scheme from a discipline
senses.titleCN: 来自某一学科的解释方案
senses.definition: a recognized explanatory scheme borrowed from a field such as psychology, economics or sociology
senses.definitionCN: 从心理学、经济学或社会学等领域借来的、被认可的解释方案
senses.example: The study used a sociological theoretical framework to explain voting.
senses.exampleCN: 这项研究用社会学的理论框架解释投票行为。
senses.why: Disciplines keep ready-made schemes, and borrowing one gives a study an established language for its findings.
senses.whyCN: 学科各自备有成套方案，借来一套就让研究结果有了既成的解释语言。

senses.title: The theory chapter of a thesis
senses.titleCN: 学位论文中的理论章节
senses.definition: the section of a thesis that reviews and justifies the theory chosen for the project
senses.definitionCN: 学位论文中评述并论证所选理论的那一部分
senses.example: Chapter two sets out the theoretical framework in twenty pages.
senses.exampleCN: 第二章用二十页篇幅交代理论框架。
senses.why: In academic writing the abstract structure becomes a named section, so the phrase also labels a chapter.
senses.whyCN: 在学术写作里，抽象结构变成一个具名章节，因此这个词组也指一章。

senses.title: A lens for reading the data
senses.definition: the perspective through which observations are selected, sorted and given meaning
senses.definitionCN: 用来筛选、归类并赋予观察以意义的视角
senses.example: Through this theoretical framework, silence in the interviews counts as data.
senses.exampleCN: 透过这个理论框架，访谈中的沉默也算作数据。
senses.why: Theory decides what counts as relevant, which is like a lens that brings one part of the field into focus.
senses.whyCN: 理论决定什么算相关，就像镜片把视野中的一部分对焦。

senses.title: A source of testable hypotheses
senses.definition: the part of a theory that predicts relationships which the study can then test
senses.definitionCN: 理论中预测各种关系、可供研究随后检验的部分
senses.example: The theoretical framework predicts that feedback raises persistence.
senses.exampleCN: 这个理论框架预测反馈会提高坚持度。
senses.why: A theory earns its place in research by making predictions, so the framework is also a hypothesis machine.
senses.whyCN: 理论靠做出预测在研究里立足，因此框架也是一台生产假设的机器。

senses.title: The boundary of a study's claims
senses.definition: the limits that theory sets on what the study can reasonably claim
senses.definitionCN: 理论为本研究可以合理主张的范围划定的界限
senses.example: The theoretical framework limits the findings to adult learners.
senses.exampleCN: 这个理论框架把结论限定在成年学习者范围内。
senses.why: A frame holds a picture inside its edges, and theory marks how far a conclusion may travel.
senses.whyCN: 画框把画面圈在边内，理论则标出结论能走多远。

senses.title: The standard for judging fit
senses.definition: the benchmark used to decide whether findings are consistent with the theory
senses.definitionCN: 用来判断研究结果是否与理论相符的基准
senses.example: Reviewers asked whether the results fit the theoretical framework.
senses.exampleCN: 审稿人追问结果是否与理论框架相符。
senses.why: Once a scheme is adopted, it becomes a yardstick, and mismatches between results and theory become visible.
senses.whyCN: 方案一旦被采用就成为尺子，结果与理论不合之处便显现出来。

intro.en: Theoretical framework pairs a Greek word for contemplative viewing with an English word for a load-bearing structure. Theory supplies the beams; framework supplies the shape that holds them together.
intro.cn: 这个词组把希腊语中表示「沉思观看」的词，与英语中表示承重结构的词配在一起。理论提供梁，框架提供把它们拢住的形状。

items.en: Theoria meant a viewing or contemplation, especially the official viewing of a sacred rite; its deeper link to a word for sight is plausible but not certain.
items.cn: 这个词指观看或沉思，尤指对宗教仪式的正式观礼；它与表示「看」的词有联系，但这一点只是推测，并非确证。

items.en: Late Latin took the Greek adjective for «belonging to viewing» and passed it to European languages as the word for theory.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语取来这个希腊形容词，义为「与观看有关的」，再传给欧洲各语言，成为「理论」一词。

items.en: English theory appeared in the sixteenth century for a speculative scheme of knowledge, as opposed to practice.
items.cn: 英语的「理论」在十六世纪出现，指与实践相对的思辨知识体系。

items.en: Framian meant to be useful or to advance, and the related noun frame named something that gives shape and support.
items.cn: 这个古英语动词意为「有用、推进」，相关名词指给出形状与支撑的东西。

items.en: Frame and work joined in the sixteenth or seventeenth century for a supporting structure; the earliest record is uncertain.
items.cn: 「框」与「工」在十六或十七世纪合成，指起支撑作用的结构；最早记录年代不确定。

items.en: Social science fixed the two words together in the twentieth century for the theory structure that a study rests on.
items.cn: 社会科学在二十世纪把这两个词固定组合，指一项研究所依托的理论结构。

note.en: The first group belongs to the theory family or merely looks similar; the second group names other kinds of research structure.
note.cn: 第一组属于「理论」同族或只是形近；第二组指其他类型的研究结构。

entries.definition: An organized set of ideas meant to explain a class of facts.
entries.definitionCN: 指用来解释一类事实的成体系观点。

entries.definition: Concerned with theory rather than practice or measurement.
entries.definitionCN: 指关涉理论而非实践或测量的。

entries.definition: A person who builds or studies theories.
entries.definitionCN: 指建构或研究理论的人。

entries.definition: A statement proved from accepted premises; it shares the viewing root.
entries.definitionCN: 指由公认前提证明的命题；与「观看」词根同源。

entries.definition: A supporting structure, whether physical or conceptual.
entries.definitionCN: 指起支撑作用的结构，可以是实物也可以是概念。

entries.definition: The study of religion; it begins with the word for god, not for viewing.
entries.definitionCN: 指宗教学；起首是「神」的词，而非「观看」。

entries.definition: A researcher's own map of concepts and their links, rather than a borrowed theory.
entries.definitionCN: 指研究者自己绘制的概念及关系图，而非借来的理论。

entries.definition: The structure that organizes how a analysis will break a problem into parts.
entries.definitionCN: 指把问题拆成部分来分析时所依的结构。

entries.definition: A simplified representation of the variables and paths a study will examine.
entries.definitionCN: 指对研究要考察的变量与路径的简化表示。

entries.definition: A whole way of thinking shared by a field, larger than one study's framework.
entries.definitionCN: 指一个领域共有的整套思维方式，比单项研究的框架更大。

entries.definition: A specific testable prediction, narrower than a framework.
entries.definitionCN: 指具体可检验的预测，比框架窄。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the load-bearing picture and the real academic phrases around theory.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用承重结构的画面，以及围绕「理论」的真实学术搭配。

normal.en: Theory is the beam and framework is the shape: neither stands without the other.
normal.cn: 理论是梁，框架是形，两者缺一都立不住。

normal.en: A framework carries weight, so a weak theory shows up as a study that sags under its own claims.
normal.cn: 框架要承重，理论一弱，研究就会在自己的结论下塌下去。

normal.en: The phrase is standard in proposals, where it names the chapter that justifies the theory.
normal.cn: 这个词组在开题报告里是标准说法，用来指论证理论的那一章。

normal.en: A theoretical framework predicts; a conceptual framework organizes. The pair is often confused.
normal.cn: 理论框架负责预测，概念框架负责组织，两者常被混用。

normal.en: The frame around a picture decides what is inside the picture.
normal.cn: 画框决定什么在画面之内。

abstract.en: A framework is visible only when something pushes against it; theory is tested by findings that do not fit.
abstract.cn: 框架只有在被推挤时才显形，理论则靠不吻合的结果来检验。

abstract.en: Every study stands inside a frame it did not build, and the frame quietly decides what counts as evidence.
abstract.cn: 每项研究都站在一个自己没搭的框架里，这个框架悄悄决定什么算证据。

abstract.en: Beams are chosen before the room is used, which is why the theory must come before the method.
abstract.cn: 梁在使用房间之前就选好，所以理论必须先于方法。

examples.en: The paper builds its theoretical framework on two competing models of memory.
examples.cn: 这篇论文把理论框架建立在两种相互竞争的记忆模型上。

examples.en: Without a theoretical framework, the interviews produced anecdotes rather than findings.
examples.cn: 没有理论框架，这些访谈只产出轶事而不是研究发现。

examples.en: The committee asked the student to align the method with the theoretical framework.
examples.cn: 委员会要求学生让方法与理论框架保持一致。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「理论」是梁，「框架」是框：先立梁再围框，一套撑起研究的骨架就是理论框架

root: 「理论」源自希腊语 theoria「观看、沉思」，经晚期拉丁语 theoreticus 进入欧洲语言。「框架」由古英语 framian「有用、推进」与 work「工、作」合成，十六七世纪起指承重结构；两个词在二十世纪社会科学中被固定组合。最早记录年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the whole structure to its edges: the guiding theory, the assumptions, a borrowed scheme, a thesis chapter, a lens on data, a source of hypotheses, the limit of claims, and the standard of fit.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从整体走向边缘：统领理论、假设与定义、借来的解释方案、论文理论章、解读数据的镜片、假设的来源、结论的边界、契合的标准。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a frame of beams is raised first, and every later panel is fixed to those beams.
core.cn: 核心意象：先立起一副梁架，此后每一块板都固定在这副梁上。

branches.en: THE GUIDING THEORY: the borrowed scheme that decides what the study examines.
branches.cn: 统领理论：决定研究考察什么的借用方案。

branches.en: THE FIXED ASSUMPTIONS: definitions and beliefs accepted before data arrive.
branches.cn: 既定假设：在数据到来前就接受的界定与信念。

branches.en: THE WRITTEN CHAPTER: the part of a thesis that justifies the choice.
branches.cn: 成文章节：论文中论证该选择的部分。

branches.en: THE WORKING LENS: the perspective that sorts data and predicts relations.
branches.cn: 工作镜片：筛选数据并预测关系的视角。

branches.en: THE EDGE OF THE FRAME: what the study may claim and how fit is judged.
branches.cn: 框的边缘：研究可以主张什么，以及如何判断契合。

intro.en: The phrase joins a Greek-derived theory word to an Old English structure word, and both halves still carry their original pictures.
intro.cn: 这个词组把希腊来源的理论词与古英语的结构词接在一起，两半至今都带着各自的原始画面。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies theoreticus; the structure half is native English and has no Latin entry.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了「理论的」这一形容词；结构那一半是英语本族词，没有拉丁语条目。

items.example: It passed through Latin into the learned word for theory.
items.exampleCN: 它经拉丁语进入学术用语「理论」。

items.example: It gave English the adjective theoretical.
items.exampleCN: 它给英语提供了形容词「理论的」。

items.example: It marks theoretical as an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 它把「理论」标为形容词。

items.example: It is the load-bearing half of the phrase.
items.exampleCN: 它是这个词组里承重的那一半。

items.example: It joins frame to form framework.
items.exampleCN: 它与「框」合成「框架」。

items.example: The earlier verb behind frame.
items.exampleCN: 这是「框」背后更早的动词。

items.example: It contrasts with theory as an organizing unit.
items.exampleCN: 它作为组织单位与「理论」相对。

items.example: It marks the neighbouring phrase conceptual framework.
items.exampleCN: 它标出邻近的「概念框架」一词。

derivatives.zh: 希腊语「观看、沉思」经拉丁语而来的名词，义为「理论」
由「理论」加形容词尾构成，义为「理论的」
加副词尾，义为「在理论上」
加从事者名词尾，义为「理论家」
加动词尾，义为「建立理论」

definition_zh: 概念框架；研究者把相关概念及其关系组织起来、用以界定范围并指导分析的结构
definition_en: a researcher's organized map of the concepts relevant to a study and the relationships among them
core_image: 白板上画着一圈圈方框，每个框里写一个概念，箭头把彼此的关系连起来，最后收束成一个整体
scene: 做质性研究的学生把访谈里反复出现的几类现象先画成方框，再用箭头标出它们的关系。The conceptual framework shows how the three factors influence one another.
sceneCN: 这里指用图示把概念与关系组织起来的框架（第 1 个义项：概念及其关系的组织图）；句意为这个概念框架显示了三个因素之间如何相互影响。

derivatives.zh: 拉丁语「 conceive」而来的名词，义为「概念」
由「概念」加形容词尾构成，义为「概念的」
加动词尾，义为「概念化；把……形成概念」
再加表示行为的名词尾，义为「概念化过程」
加副词尾，义为「在概念上」

senses.title: A map of concepts and their links
senses.definition: a diagram or scheme that places the key concepts of a study and draws the links between them
senses.definitionCN: 把研究的关键概念摆出来并画出彼此关系的图式或方案
senses.example: The conceptual framework places trust between communication and cooperation.
senses.exampleCN: 这个概念框架把信任放在沟通与合作之间。
senses.why: A map is not the land, but it fixes which places connect, and the phrase does exactly that for ideas.
senses.whyCN: 地图不是土地，却固定了哪些地方相连，这个词组对观念做的正是这件事。

senses.title: The researcher's own synthesis
senses.definition: the arrangement the researcher builds from the literature rather than a scheme borrowed whole
senses.definitionCN: 研究者从文献中自行搭建的安排，而非整套搬用的方案
senses.example: Her conceptual framework grew out of five years of field notes.
senses.exampleCN: 她的概念框架是从五年的田野笔记里长出来的。
senses.why: Theoretical frameworks are borrowed, but conceptual ones are assembled, which is why the possessive «her» matters.
senses.whyCN: 理论框架是借的，概念框架是拼的，所以这里用「她的」来限定。

senses.title: A diagram of the variables
senses.definition: a visual arrangement of variables and arrows that shows expected directions of influence
senses.definitionCN: 把变量与箭头排成图，显示预期的影响方向
senses.example: The conceptual framework puts the mediator in the middle of the diagram.
senses.exampleCN: 这个概念框架把中介变量放在图示中央。
senses.why: Arrows carry direction, and a framework drawn with arrows reads almost like a claim about cause.
senses.whyCN: 箭头带方向，用箭头画出的框架读起来几乎就是对因果的主张。

senses.title: The set of constructs to be measured
senses.definition: the defined constructs that the study will turn into measures or interview codes
senses.definitionCN: 研究将转化为测量指标或访谈编码的、已界定的构念
senses.example: Each box in the conceptual framework became a scale in the questionnaire.
senses.exampleCN: 概念框架里的每个方框都变成了问卷中的一张量表。
senses.why: What is drawn must eventually be measured, so the framework also lists the constructs that need instruments.
senses.whyCN: 画出来的东西最终要能被测量，因此框架也列出需要工具去测的构念。

senses.title: The scheme for coding qualitative data
senses.definition: the analytic scheme that guides how interviews or observations are sorted into categories
senses.definitionCN: 指导如何把访谈或观察归入各类别的分析方案
senses.example: The coder used the conceptual framework to group the responses.
senses.exampleCN: 编码员用这个概念框架给回答分组。
senses.why: In qualitative work the framework becomes a set of boxes that the raw talk is sorted into.
senses.whyCN: 在质性研究里，框架变成一组方框，原始话语被分装进去。

senses.title: The stated scope of the study
senses.definition: the boundary that the framework draws around what the study will and will not examine
senses.definitionCN: 框架为研究划定考察与不考察范围的边界
senses.example: The conceptual framework excludes firms with fewer than ten staff.
senses.exampleCN: 这个概念框架把不足十人的企业排除在外。
senses.why: A frame has edges, and stating the concepts also states what is left outside them.
senses.whyCN: 框有边，界定概念的同时也界定了框外之物。

senses.title: The framework section of a proposal
senses.titleCN: 研究计划中的框架部分
senses.definition: the written part of a proposal that presents and justifies the concept map
senses.definitionCN: 研究计划中呈现并论证概念图的书面部分
senses.example: The conceptual framework takes four pages of the proposal.
senses.exampleCN: 概念框架在研究计划里占了四页。
senses.why: A drawing needs a caption, and academic writing turns the drawing into a named section.
senses.whyCN: 图需要说明文字，学术写作便把这张图变成一个具名章节。

senses.title: A guide for programme design
senses.definition: the concept scheme used to plan a policy, service or intervention outside pure research
senses.definitionCN: 用于在纯研究之外规划政策、服务或干预的概念方案
senses.example: The agency adopted the conceptual framework when it redesigned the service.
senses.exampleCN: 该机构在重新设计服务时采用了这个概念框架。
senses.why: The same map that organizes research can organize action, because both need to know which factors connect.
senses.whyCN: 组织研究的那张图也能组织行动，因为两者都需要知道哪些因素相连。

intro.en: Conceptual framework joins a Latin word for a conceived idea with an English word for a supporting structure. It names the map a researcher builds before the measuring begins.
intro.cn: 这个词组把拉丁语中表示「被构想出的观念」的词，与英语中表示承重结构的词接在一起，指研究者在开始测量之前搭好的那张图。

items.en: Capere meant to take or seize, and with the prefix com- it produced concipere, to take in and conceive.
items.cn: 这个词根意为「拿、抓」，加上表示「共同」的前缀后构成「收进、孕育」，即构想。

items.en: Conceptus named a taking in, hence a conceived idea; English concept arrived through French in the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 这个词指「收进」，因而指被构想出的观念；英语的「概念」经法语在十六世纪进入。

items.en: The adjective conceptual appeared in the seventeenth century for what exists in the mind rather than in the hand.
items.cn: 形容词「概念的」在十七世纪出现，指存在于头脑而非手中的东西。

items.en: Frame named a structure that gives shape and support, and its verb meant to construct.
items.cn: 这个词指给出形状与支撑的结构，其动词义为建造。

items.en: The compound appeared in the sixteenth or seventeenth century for a skeletal support; the exact first record is uncertain.
items.cn: 这个复合词在十六或十七世纪出现，指骨架式的支撑；确切最早记录不确定。

items.en: Research methods texts fixed conceptual framework as the researcher's own map, distinct from a borrowed theoretical framework.
items.cn: 研究方法教材把「概念框架」固定为研究者自绘的图，与借用的「理论框架」相区别。

note.en: The first group belongs to the concept family or looks similar; the second group names neighbouring research structures.
note.cn: 第一组属于「概念」同族或形近；第二组指相邻的研究结构。

entries.definition: A general idea formed by taking the shared features of many cases.
entries.definitionCN: 指从众多事例的共同点中形成的一般观念。

entries.definition: Existing in thought or organized around concepts.
entries.definitionCN: 指存在于思想中或以概念组织的。

entries.definition: To form a concept of something or to describe it in conceptual terms.
entries.definitionCN: 指对某物形成概念或以概念方式描述。

entries.definition: The act of forming an idea, or the idea formed.
entries.definitionCN: 指形成观念的行为或所形成的观念。

entries.definition: A supporting structure, physical or conceptual.
entries.definitionCN: 指支撑结构，可为实物或概念。

entries.definition: To leave out; it looks like concept but comes from a taking-out prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 指排除在外；形近但来自「取出」的前缀。

entries.definition: A theory structure borrowed from a field, which a study then applies.
entries.definitionCN: 指从某一领域借来、由研究加以应用的理论结构。

entries.definition: The structure that shows how a problem will be broken into analysable parts.
entries.definitionCN: 指显示如何把问题拆成可分析部分的结构。

entries.definition: A simplified formal representation of variables and their paths.
entries.definitionCN: 指变量及其路径的简化形式表示。

entries.definition: A field-wide way of thinking, broader than a single study's map.
entries.definitionCN: 指领域层面的整套思维方式，比单项研究的图更宽。

entries.definition: A defined attribute that a study intends to measure.
entries.definitionCN: 指研究打算测量的、已界定的属性。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the whiteboard picture, the real distinction from a theoretical framework, and the measurement link.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用白板画图的画面、与理论框架的真实区别，以及通向测量的一环。

normal.en: Concept gives the boxes; framework gives the arrows and the edges.
normal.cn: 概念提供方框，框架提供箭头与边界。

normal.en: Conceptual frameworks are built, not borrowed, which is why they belong to a named researcher.
normal.cn: 概念框架是搭建的而非借用的，所以它属于某个具体研究者。

normal.en: Every box on the board should later become a measure, a code or a hypothesis.
normal.cn: 板上的每个方框后来都该变成一项测量、一个编码或一条假设。

normal.en: The theoretical framework supplies the theory; the conceptual framework supplies the arrangement.
normal.cn: 理论框架提供理论，概念框架提供排列方式。

normal.en: A map with arrows already whispers a claim about which way influence runs.
normal.cn: 带箭头的图已经在暗示影响朝哪个方向流动。

abstract.en: A conceptual framework is a promise that everything drawn will eventually be either measured or explained.
abstract.cn: 概念框架是一份承诺：画出的每样东西最终要么被测量，要么被解释。

abstract.en: Two researchers can share the same theory and still draw different maps, which shows the map is the person.
abstract.cn: 两位研究者可以共用一套理论却画出不同的图，说明图就是人本身。

abstract.en: The frame is drawn before the evidence arrives, and that order is what makes it a frame rather than a summary.
abstract.cn: 框架在证据到来之前就画好，正是这个顺序使它成为框架而不是总结。

examples.en: The conceptual framework groups motivation, opportunity and ability under one scheme.
examples.cn: 这个概念框架把动机、机会与能力归入同一套方案。

examples.en: She revised the conceptual framework after the first round of interviews.
examples.cn: 第一轮访谈之后，她修订了概念框架。

examples.en: The diagram in the conceptual framework became the basis for the questionnaire.
examples.cn: 概念框架中的图示成了问卷设计的基础。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「概念」是框里的字，「框架」是框本身：把概念装进框、用箭头连起来，就是概念框架

root: 「概念」源自拉丁语 concipere「收进、孕育」，其词根为 capere「抓取」；「框架」由古英语 framian「有用、推进」与 work 合成。二十世纪研究方法文献把「概念框架」固定为研究者自绘的概念关系图。最早记录年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the map itself to its practical uses: the concept map, the researcher's synthesis, the variable diagram, the constructs to measure, the coding scheme, the scope, the proposal section, and the design guide.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从图本身走向实际用途：概念关系图、研究者的综合、变量图示、待测构念、编码方案、研究范围、计划章节、设计指南。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: boxes are drawn on a board and arrows are added until the separate ideas read as one structure.
core.cn: 核心意象：白板上先画方框，再补箭头，直到分开的观念读起来像一个整体。

branches.en: THE BUILT MAP: concepts placed and linked by the researcher's own synthesis.
branches.cn: 搭建的图：由研究者自行综合摆放并连接的概念。

branches.en: THE ARROWED DIAGRAM: variables arranged with expected directions of influence.
branches.cn: 带箭头的图：变量按预期影响方向排列。

branches.en: THE MEASURABLE SIDE: constructs turned into scales and codes.
branches.cn: 可测量的一面：构念转化为量表与编码。

branches.en: THE STATED EDGES: the scope that is drawn and then written into the proposal.
branches.cn: 明示的边缘：画出范围，再写进研究计划。

branches.en: THE OUTWARD USE: the same map guiding a service or policy design.
branches.cn: 向外的用途：同一张图指导服务或政策设计。

intro.en: Conceptual framework joins a Latin idea word to an Old English structure word; both halves keep their original pictures.
intro.cn: 这个词组把拉丁语的观念词与古英语的结构词接起来，两半都保留着原始画面。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies concipere and conceptus; the structure half is native English and has no Latin entry.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了「构想」与「概念」两词；结构那一半是英语本族词，没有拉丁语条目。

items.example: It turns taking into taking in.
items.exampleCN: 它把「拿」变成「收进来」。

items.example: The root behind concept and capture.
items.exampleCN: 这是「概念」与「捕获」共同的词根。

items.example: The direct source of the idea word.
items.exampleCN: 这是观念词的直接来源。

items.example: It became English concept.
items.exampleCN: 它成为英语的「概念」。

items.example: It forms conceptual from the noun.
items.exampleCN: 它由名词构成形容词「概念的」。

items.example: The load-bearing half of the phrase.
items.exampleCN: 它是词组里承重的那一半。

items.example: It joins frame to make framework.
items.exampleCN: 它与「框」合成「框架」。

items.example: The verb built on the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这是由该形容词构成的动词。

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语「被构想出的观念」经法语而来，义为「概念」
加形容词尾，义为「概念的」
加动词尾，义为「概念化」
加行为名词尾，义为「概念化过程」
加副词尾，义为「在概念上」

definition_zh: 前提；前提假设；（复数）房屋及场地；法律文书开头陈述的事实；以……为前提预先提出
definition_en: a statement accepted as true and used as the basis of an argument, or (in the plural) a building and its land
core_image: 长桌的四条桌腿先稳稳立住，桌面上才摆得下一层层叠起的论证卡片
scene: 辩论开始前，主持人提醒双方先确认共同接受的基本判断，否则后面的推论都无处落脚。The whole argument rests on a premise that nobody has tested.
sceneCN: 这里指论证所依据的基本判断（第 1 个义项：作为论证基础的前提命题）；句意为整个论证都建立在一个无人检验过的前提上。

pos.zh: 前提；前提假设；（复数）房屋及场地
以……为前提预先提出（较少用）

derivatives.zh: 复数形式，义为「房屋及场地；营业场所」
由动词加已然词尾构成，义为「以……为基础的」
逻辑学中的另一种拼写，义同「前提」
由「前提」与「基于」复合而成，义为「以前提为基础的」

senses.title: A proposition that supports an argument
senses.definition: a statement put forward as true so that a conclusion can be drawn from it
senses.definitionCN: 作为真实陈述提出、以便从中推出结论的命题
senses.example: The main premise of the essay is that prices reflect information.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章的主要前提是价格反映信息。
senses.why: The Latin word meant something sent before, and this sense places the statement ahead of the conclusion.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁词本义是「事先送出之物」，这一义项把它放在结论之前。

senses.title: An assumption taken without proof
senses.titleCN: 未加证明就接受的假设
senses.definition: a belief that a study or person accepts as true without testing it
senses.definitionCN: 研究或个人未经检验就当作真实的信念
senses.example: The model works only if its premise about human rationality holds.
senses.exampleCN: 只有当模型关于人类理性的假设成立时，它才有效。
senses.why: What is put before an argument is often simply granted, which is how a premise becomes an assumption.
senses.whyCN: 放在论证之前的东西常被直接认可，「前提」由此变成「假设」。

senses.title: The major premise of a syllogism
senses.definition: the general statement from which a syllogism begins, before the minor premise is applied
senses.definitionCN: 三段论起始的一般性陈述，在其后接上小前提
senses.example: The major premise says all mammals are warm-blooded.
senses.exampleCN: 大前提说所有哺乳动物都是温血的。
senses.why: Logic gave the word a fixed slot: the general claim sits first, and the specific case is placed under it.
senses.whyCN: 逻辑学给这个词一个固定位置：一般性主张坐第一，具体事例被置于其下。

senses.title: The minor premise of a syllogism
senses.definition: the specific statement that brings a particular case under the general one
senses.definitionCN: 把具体事例归入一般陈述之下的特定陈述
senses.example: The minor premise states that this animal is a mammal.
senses.exampleCN: 小前提陈述这只动物是哺乳动物。
senses.why: The second slot in the syllogism is also called a premise, since both statements must be granted before the conclusion.
senses.whyCN: 三段论中的第二个位置同样称为前提，因为两个陈述都必须先被认可，结论才成立。

senses.title: A building and its land
senses.definition: the buildings and the ground belonging to a business or an owner, used in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 属于某企业或业主的建筑物与土地，用复数形式
senses.example: The inspectors walked through the factory premises.
senses.exampleCN: 检查人员走遍了工厂的场地。
senses.why: Legal deeds opened by describing the property set before the reader, and that list of property became the buildings themselves.
senses.whyCN: 法律契约开头先描述摆在读者面前的财产，这份财产清单后来就指建筑物本身。

senses.title: The property recited in a deed
senses.titleCN: 法律文书开头陈述的财产
senses.definition: the opening part of a legal instrument that sets out the facts and property concerned
senses.definitionCN: 法律文书开头说明相关事实与财产的部分
senses.example: The lease recites the premises before stating the rent.
senses.exampleCN: 这份租约在说明租金之前先陈述标的财产。
senses.why: The word names what is placed in front of the operative clauses, so it labels that opening recital.
senses.whyCN: 这个词指放在操作性条款之前的内容，因此用来指开头的陈述部分。

senses.title: A condition treated as given
senses.titleCN: 模型中当作给定的条件
senses.definition: a condition that a model or calculation accepts as fixed before it begins
senses.definitionCN: 模型或计算在开始之前就当作固定条件的设定
senses.example: The estimate rests on the premise that fuel prices stay flat.
senses.exampleCN: 这一估算建立在燃料价格持平的假设之上。
senses.why: A model must fix something before it can move, and whatever is fixed is literally placed in front.
senses.whyCN: 模型必须先固定某些东西才能运转，被固定者正被摆在最前面。

senses.title: A claim a debate must grant
senses.titleCN: 辩论中须先接受的主张
senses.definition: a statement that one side asks the other to accept before the exchange can proceed
senses.definitionCN: 一方要求另一方在交锋开始前先接受的主张
senses.example: The judge asked whether both sides shared that premise.
senses.exampleCN: 主持人问双方是否共有那个前提。
senses.why: Debate is an argument built in public, so it needs a floor of agreed statements under it.
senses.whyCN: 辩论是当众搭建的论证，因此需要一层公认陈述作地板。

senses.title: To state something beforehand
senses.definition: to set something out in advance as a basis for what follows
senses.definitionCN: 事先把某内容摆出来，作为后续论述的基础
senses.example: Let me premise my answer with one condition.
senses.exampleCN: 请允许我先以一个条件作为回答的前提。
senses.why: The verb kept the Latin sense of sending something ahead, and English uses it rarely, mostly in formal prose.
senses.whyCN: 动词保留了拉丁语「事先送出」的意思，英语中很少用，多见于正式书面语。

intro.en: Premise comes from Latin praemissa, things sent before, from praemittere, to send ahead. Logic took the word for the statements placed before a conclusion, and law took it for the property described at the start of a deed; the plural then became the buildings themselves.
intro.cn: 这个词来自拉丁语 praemissa「事先送出之物」，出自动词「预先送出」。逻辑学用它指放在结论之前的陈述，法律用它指契约开头描述的财产，其复数随后就指建筑物本身。

items.en: Mittere meant to send or let go, and it stands behind words of sending, such as mission and transmit.
items.cn: 这个词根意为「送、放出」，英语中表示发送的词多出自它。

items.en: The prefix prae- added «in front», so the verb meant to send something ahead of what follows.
items.cn: 前缀加上「在前」，于是动词意为把某物先于后续内容送出去。

items.en: The neuter plural named the things set before a conclusion, and logic adopted it as a technical term.
items.cn: 中性复数指放在结论之前的内容，逻辑学把它采用为术语。

items.en: Translations of Aristotle fixed major and minor premise as the two statements above and below the conclusion.
items.cn: 对亚里士多德著作的翻译固定了「大前提」与「小前提」，即结论之上与之下的两个陈述。

items.en: Deeds opened by reciting the property, and the plural premises came to mean that property and then the buildings on it.
items.cn: 契约开头先陈述财产，复数形式便指该财产，随后又指其上的建筑物。

items.en: The building sense now lives almost entirely in the plural, while the logic sense keeps the singular; the split's exact date is uncertain.
items.cn: 建筑物义如今几乎只存在于复数，逻辑义则保留单数；两者分开的确切年代不确定。

note.en: The first group shares the same Latin root or looks close; the second group names other starting points of reasoning.
note.cn: 第一组共享同一拉丁词根或形近；第二组指推理的其他起点。

entries.definition: The plural noun for a building and its land, from the property clause of a deed.
entries.definitionCN: 指房屋及场地，来自契约中的财产条款。

entries.definition: Based on a stated assumption; the past participle used as an adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 指以某陈述假设为基础的，是过去分词作形容词。

entries.definition: The older spelling used in logic for a stated proposition.
entries.definitionCN: 逻辑学中指前提命题的旧拼写。

entries.definition: First in rank; it belongs to the Latin word for first, not to sending ahead.
entries.definitionCN: 指地位最高的；属于拉丁语「第一」，与「预先送出」无关。

entries.definition: A bonus or an insurance payment; it comes from the word for reward.
entries.definitionCN: 指奖金或保险费；来自表示报酬的词。

entries.definition: A declaration that one will do something; its root is to send forth a word, a different verb.
entries.definitionCN: 指表示将做某事的声明；其词根是「送出话语」，属另一动词。

entries.definition: Something accepted as true without evidence, often silently.
entries.definitionCN: 指无证据而被接受为真的东西，常是默许的。

entries.definition: A belief that must already hold for a statement to make sense.
entries.definitionCN: 指一个陈述要成立就必须先已存在的信念。

entries.definition: A statement that can be judged true or false.
entries.definitionCN: 指可判断真假的陈述。

entries.definition: A tentative explanation offered for testing, not merely granted.
entries.definitionCN: 指提出来供检验的暂时解释，而不只是被认可。

entries.definition: A principle accepted without proof as a starting point.
entries.definitionCN: 指无需证明即被接受作为出发点的原理。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the table-leg picture, the syllogism slots, the legal deed and the everyday plural.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用桌腿画面、三段论的两个位置、法律契约与日常复数用法。

normal.en: A premise is sent before the conclusion, just as a table leg is placed before the table top.
normal.cn: 前提先于结论送出，正如桌腿先于桌面立好。

normal.en: The major premise is the wide statement; the minor premise puts one case under it.
normal.cn: 大前提是宽的一般陈述，小前提把一个事例放到它下面。

normal.en: Premises in the plural are buildings, from the property clause at the head of a deed.
normal.cn: 复数形式指建筑物，来自契约开头的财产条款。

normal.en: A false premise makes a valid argument reach a wrong conclusion.
normal.cn: 前提错了，形式有效的论证也会得出错误结论。

normal.en: On the premise that is the everyday phrase that carries the logic sense into ordinary writing.
normal.cn: 「以……为前提」是把逻辑义带入日常写作的固定说法。

abstract.en: A premise is a floor that nobody looks at until the argument falls through it.
abstract.cn: 前提是一块地板，直到论证掉了下去，才有人低头看它。

abstract.en: Every model stands on statements it never proves, and that silence is what makes it usable.
abstract.cn: 每个模型都站在它从不证明的陈述上，正是这份沉默让它可用。

abstract.en: The same word can name a sentence and a building, because both are things set in front of you.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既能指一句话，也能指一栋楼，因为两者都是摆在你面前的东西。

examples.en: The study rests on the premise that memory declines with age.
examples.cn: 这项研究建立在记忆随年龄衰退这一前提上。

examples.en: If the premise is false, the conclusion cannot stand.
examples.cn: 如果前提错误，结论就站不住。

examples.en: Visitors must not smoke anywhere on the premises.
examples.cn: 访客不得在场地内任何地方吸烟。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「普瑞密斯」——「普」通人先「密」密接受的那句话，就是推理的前提

root: 拉丁语 praemissa「事先送出之物」← praemittere「预先送出」= prae-「在前」+ mittere「送、放」。逻辑学经中世纪翻译固定「大前提、小前提」，法律契约开头的财产陈述引申出「房屋及场地」。十五世纪起见于英语；两义分化的确切年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses run from logic to property: a supporting proposition, an untested assumption, the major and minor premises, buildings and land, a deed recital, a fixed model condition, a debated claim, and the rare verb.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项从逻辑延伸到财产：支撑命题、未验证假设、大前提、小前提、房屋场地、契约陈述、模型条件、辩论主张，以及少用的动词义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: four legs are set down first, and only then can the stacked cards of argument rest on the top.
core.cn: 核心意象：先放下四条桌腿，论证的卡片堆才放得上桌面。

branches.en: THE ARGUMENT FLOOR: the proposition that must be granted before debate can proceed.
branches.cn: 论证的地板：辩论开始前必须先被认可的那个命题。

branches.en: THE UNPROVED GRANT: assumptions that a person or a model simply accepts.
branches.cn: 未经证明的认可：人或模型直接接受的假设。

branches.en: THE TWO LOGIC SLOTS: the general statement and the case placed under it.
branches.cn: 逻辑的两个位置：一般陈述与置于其下的事例。

branches.en: THE LEGAL PROPERTY: the recited property and the buildings standing on it.
branches.cn: 法律上的财产：契约陈述的财产及其上的建筑物。

branches.en: THE RARE VERB: to send a condition ahead as a basis.
branches.cn: 少用的动词义：事先把一个条件送出作为基础。

intro.en: Premise is a Latin participle turned noun, and the same root that sends things ahead also produced words of mission and transmission.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语分词转成的名词，同一个「预先送出」词根也产生了「使命」「传送」等词。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies praemittere and praemissa; the logic and property senses both grew from the idea of things placed in front.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了「预先送出」与「事先送出之物」；逻辑义与财产义都从「摆在前面之物」长出来。

items.example: It marks what is sent ahead.
items.exampleCN: 它标出事先送出的东西。

items.example: The root of mission and transmit.
items.exampleCN: 这是「使命」与「传送」的词根。

items.example: The direct source of the noun.
items.exampleCN: 这是该名词的直接来源。

items.example: It became the logic term for a premise.
items.exampleCN: 它成为逻辑术语「前提」。

items.example: It marks the rare English verb premise.
items.exampleCN: 它标明这个少用的英语动词。

items.example: The legal sense moved into everyday property talk.
items.exampleCN: 法律义进入日常财产用语。

items.meaning: a statement set before a conclusion
items.example: The everyday singular that carries the logic sense.
items.exampleCN: 这是承载逻辑义的日常单数形式。

items.example: It survives chiefly in British academic prose.
items.exampleCN: 它主要保留在英国学术写作中。

derivatives.zh: 复数形式，义为「房屋及场地」
加已然词尾，义为「以……为基础的」
逻辑学旧拼写，义为「前提」
复合形容词，义为「以前提为基础的」

definition_zh: 断言；主张；陈述；对权利或权威的维护；程序中的断言检查
definition_en: a confident and forceful statement of fact or belief, or the act of stating or defending something
core_image: 一个人把一枚印章重重按在文件上，抬手时印痕已经固定，再难悄悄收回
scene: 审稿人指出，论文里那句强硬的判断并没有数据支撑，只能算是一种声明。The claim remained an assertion until the data arrived.
sceneCN: 这里指没有数据支撑的强硬判断（第 1 个义项：自信的断言）；句意为在数据到手之前，那个说法始终只是一句断言。

pos.zh: 断言；主张；维护；断言语句

derivatives.zh: 由同一拉丁词干构成的动词，义为「断言；维护」
由动词加表示「倾向」的形容词尾构成，义为「自信的；坚定主张的」
加副词尾，义为「断然地」
加表示性质的名词尾，义为「自信果断」
加已然词尾，义为「已断言的；被主张的」

senses.title: A confident statement of fact
senses.definition: a firm statement that something is true, made without hesitation
senses.definitionCN: 毫不迟疑地断定某事为真的陈述
senses.example: Her assertion that the test had failed was later confirmed.
senses.exampleCN: 她关于测试失败的那句断言后来得到证实。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to claim as one's own, and a claim made firmly becomes a statement of fact.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词意为「认作自己的」，坚定地认领就成了一种事实陈述。

senses.title: A claim open to challenge
senses.definition: a statement put forward as true that others may reasonably dispute
senses.definitionCN: 被提出为真、但他人可以合理反驳的陈述
senses.example: The report's central assertion has no data behind it.
senses.exampleCN: 报告的核心主张背后没有数据。
senses.why: Anything asserted invites a counter-statement, so the word often marks a claim still awaiting proof.
senses.whyCN: 凡是断言都会招来反陈述，因此这个词常标出尚待证明的主张。

senses.title: A declaration of rights
senses.definition: the act of stating or defending a right, title or claim
senses.definitionCN: 声明或维护某项权利、名分或主张的行为
senses.example: The march was an assertion of the right to assemble.
senses.exampleCN: 那场游行是对集会权利的一次声明。
senses.why: Rights are claimed before they are used, and the word covers that public claiming.
senses.whyCN: 权利在被使用之前先被主张，这个词覆盖这种公开主张。

senses.title: A proposition affirmed in logic
senses.definition: a proposition that is put forward as true and from which inferences may follow
senses.definitionCN: 被提出为真、并可据以推出结论的命题
senses.example: In the proof, each assertion must follow from the one before.
senses.exampleCN: 在证明中，每个命题都必须由前一个推出。
senses.why: Logic treats an assertion as a statement with a truth value, which is a formal version of claiming.
senses.whyCN: 逻辑学把断言看作有真值的陈述，这是「主张」的形式化版本。

senses.title: An assertion in a program
senses.definition: a statement in code that declares a condition which must be true at that point
senses.definitionCN: 代码中声明某条件在该处必须为真的语句
senses.example: The developer added an assertion to catch empty input.
senses.exampleCN: 开发者在代码里加了一个断言，用来捕获空输入。
senses.why: Programming borrowed the word because a check asserts that a condition holds, and fails loudly if it does not.
senses.whyCN: 编程借用这个词，因为检查是在断言某条件成立，不成立就大声报错。

senses.title: A forceful expression of opinion
senses.definition: a confident way of saying what one thinks, often in speech
senses.definitionCN: 以自信的方式说出自己的想法，常见于口头表达
senses.example: His assertion that the plan was hopeless silenced the room.
senses.exampleCN: 他那句计划毫无希望的说法让全场安静下来。
senses.why: Tone matters here: the noun can name the force of a statement as much as its content.
senses.whyCN: 语气在这里很关键：这个名词既指内容，也指说话的力度。

senses.title: An assertion of authority
senses.definition: the act of showing or enforcing one's power or control
senses.definitionCN: 展示或强行施加自身权力与控制的行为
senses.example: The new manager's first meeting was an assertion of control.
senses.exampleCN: 新任经理的第一次会议是一次掌控权的宣示。
senses.why: Power is often claimed before it is obeyed, and the word names that claim.
senses.whyCN: 权力常在被服从之前先被主张，这个词就指那种主张。

senses.title: A statement made without proof
senses.definition: a statement offered as true although no evidence has been supplied
senses.definitionCN: 虽无证据却作为真实提出的陈述
senses.example: The essay opens with an assertion rather than a finding.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章以一个断言而不是发现开头。
senses.why: Because the word does not itself guarantee proof, it can politely name something unproven.
senses.whyCN: 因为这个词本身不保证有证明，它可以客气地指称未经证实的东西。

intro.en: Assertion comes from Latin asserere, to claim or maintain, literally to join something to oneself. The noun entered English through French and kept both the sense of a firm statement and the sense of defending a right.
intro.cn: 这个词来自拉丁语 asserere「主张、维护」，字面意为「把某物接到自己身上」。名词经法语进入英语，既保留「坚定陈述」的意思，也保留「维护权利」的意思。

items.en: Serere meant to join or arrange in a row, and it also gave the words for series and insert.
items.cn: 这个词根意为「连接、排成行」，也表示「系列」与「插入」的词也出自它。

items.en: With the prefix ad-, the verb meant to join to oneself, hence to claim a thing as one's own and defend it.
items.cn: 加上表示「朝向」的前缀后，动词意为「接到自己身上」，因而指把某物认作自己的并加以维护。

items.en: Roman law used the verb for asserting freedom or a right, and English kept that public, declarative force.
items.cn: 罗马法用这个动词表示主张自由或权利，英语保留了这种公开宣告的力量。

items.en: The noun assertion appeared in English writing on logic and law; its exact first record is uncertain.
items.cn: 名词「断言」在十五世纪的逻辑与法律写作中出现；确切最早记录不确定。

items.en: Grammar calls a positive statement an assertive sentence, and logic treats assertions as propositions with truth values.
items.cn: 语法学把肯定陈述称为断言句，逻辑学把断言当作有真值的命题。

items.en: Programming languages adopted assertion for a condition the program declares must hold at a given point.
items.cn: 编程语言采用这个词，指程序声明在某处必须成立的条件。

note.en: The first group shares the joining root or looks similar; the second group names statements and claims of other strengths.
note.cn: 第一组共享「连接」词根或形近；第二组指力度不同的陈述与主张。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to state firmly or to defend a right.
entries.definitionCN: 指坚定陈述或维护权利的动词。

entries.definition: Confident and direct in stating one's views.
entries.definitionCN: 指陈述观点时自信直接的。

entries.definition: The quality of standing up for oneself calmly and directly.
entries.definitionCN: 指平静而直接地维护自身立场的品质。

entries.definition: To put something inside; same joining root, inward prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 指把某物放入；与断言共享「连接」词根，前缀向内。

entries.definition: To abandon; the prefix means apart, so the joining is undone.
entries.definitionCN: 指抛弃；前缀意为「分开」，即把连接解开。

entries.definition: The noun itself, naming both the act and the statement.
entries.definitionCN: 指该名词本身，兼指行为与所说内容。

entries.definition: A statement that something is true, often one not yet proved.
entries.definitionCN: 指声称某事为真，常指尚未证明的说法。

entries.definition: A formal public statement, stronger in official weight than in proof.
entries.definitionCN: 指正式的公开声明，官方分量重于证明。

entries.definition: The neutral word for something said or written.
entries.definitionCN: 指说出或写下的内容，是中性的说法。

entries.definition: A point argued in a debate or essay.
entries.definitionCN: 指辩论或文章中提出的论点。

entries.definition: A positive statement that something is true, often in law or religion.
entries.definitionCN: 指肯定某事为真的陈述，常用于法律或宗教。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the stamp picture, the legal claim of a right and the programming statement.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用盖章的画面、对权利的法律主张以及程序中的断言语句。

normal.en: To assert is to claim something as one's own, which is why the word can mean both saying and defending.
normal.cn: 断言就是把某物认作自己的，所以这个词既能指说出，也能指维护。

normal.en: An assertion is a stamp pressed down: the mark is made before anyone can argue with it.
normal.cn: 断言是按下的一枚印章：印痕在别人反驳之前就已经留下。

normal.en: Assertive speech is confident speech, and assertiveness training teaches people to state needs plainly.
normal.cn: 断言式说话就是自信的说话，「自信训练」教人把需求讲清楚。

normal.en: In code, an assertion is a promise that a condition holds, and a failed assertion stops the program.
normal.cn: 在代码里，断言是「某条件成立」的承诺，断言失败会中止程序。

normal.en: Assertion of rights is a fixed legal phrase, showing that the word kept its declarative legal force.
normal.cn: 「权利的主张」是固定法律说法，说明这个词保留了宣告式的法律力量。

abstract.en: An assertion is a claim wearing the clothes of a fact, and the clothes are what listeners must see through.
abstract.cn: 断言是一个穿着事实外衣的主张，而听众要做的正是看穿这件外衣。

abstract.en: Every field has its own way of stamping: logic stamps truth values, law stamps rights, code stamps conditions.
abstract.cn: 每个领域都有自己的盖章方式：逻辑盖真值，法律盖权利，代码盖条件。

abstract.en: The word reminds us that before evidence arrives, all we have is someone standing behind a sentence.
abstract.cn: 这个词提醒我们，在证据到来之前，我们只有某个人站在一句话后面。

examples.en: The author's assertion about rising costs is supported by three surveys.
examples.cn: 作者关于成本上升的断言得到三项调查的支持。

examples.en: No one could disprove his assertion that the method was safe.
examples.cn: 没有人能反驳他关于该方法安全的断言。

examples.en: The code contains an assertion that the list is never empty.
examples.cn: 这段代码里有一个断言，声明该列表永不为空。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「阿瑟申」——把话「申」明得像盖了章，一口咬定，就是断言

root: 拉丁语 asserere「主张、维护」= ad-「朝向」+ serere「连接、排成行」，字面为「接到自己身上」。罗马法用它表示主张自由或权利；名词经法语于十五世纪进入英语，兼指坚定陈述与权利维护；二十世纪编程语言又借它指断言语句。最早记录年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses run from speech act to code: a confident statement, a challengeable claim, a declaration of rights, a logical proposition, a program assertion, a forceful opinion, a show of authority, and an unproved statement.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从言语行为延伸到代码：自信陈述、可质疑的主张、权利声明、逻辑命题、程序断言、有力的意见、权威的彰显、无证明的陈述。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a seal is pressed hard onto paper, and the mark stays after the hand lifts.
core.cn: 核心意象：印章重重压上纸面，手抬起后印痕仍在。

branches.en: THE STAMPED SENTENCE: a firm statement that may or may not have proof behind it.
branches.cn: 盖章的句子：坚定的陈述，背后未必有证明。

branches.en: THE OPEN CLAIM: a statement that invites others to dispute it.
branches.cn: 敞开的主张：招来他人反驳的陈述。

branches.en: THE CLAIMED RIGHT: a right declared in public, and power shown by assertion.
branches.cn: 被主张的权利：公开宣告的权利，以及以断言彰显的权力。

branches.en: THE LOGICAL PROPOSITION: a statement carrying a truth value.
branches.cn: 逻辑命题：带有真值的陈述。

branches.en: THE CODE CHECK AND THE FORCEFUL TONE: a condition declared in code, and the weight of confident speech.
branches.cn: 代码检查与有力语气：在代码中声明的条件，以及自信说话的重量。

intro.en: Assertion is a Latin verb turned noun whose root of joining still appears in English words of insertion and series.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语动词转成的名词，其「连接」词根至今仍出现在表示插入与系列的英语词中。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies serere and asserere; the noun came through French and kept the legal flavour of claiming a right.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了「连接」与「主张」两词；名词经法语而来，保留了「主张权利」的法律意味。

items.example: It turns joining into joining to oneself.
items.exampleCN: 它把「连接」变成「接到自己身上」。

items.meaning: to join, arrange in a row
items.example: The root of insert and series.
items.exampleCN: 这是「插入」与「系列」的词根。

items.example: The direct source of the English noun.
items.exampleCN: 这是英语名词的直接来源。

items.example: It forms assertion from the verb stem.
items.exampleCN: 它由动词词干构成「断言」。

items.example: The form ad- takes before s.
items.exampleCN: 这是「朝向」前缀在 s 前的变体。

items.example: It forms assertive from the verb.
items.exampleCN: 它由动词构成形容词「自信主张的」。

items.example: It forms assertiveness.
items.exampleCN: 它构成「自信果断」这一名词。

items.example: It forms the adjective asserted.
items.exampleCN: 它构成形容词「被主张的」。

derivatives.zh: 同词干动词，义为「断言；维护」
加倾向形容词尾，义为「自信坚定的」
加副词尾，义为「断然地」
加性质名词尾，义为「自信果断」
加已然词尾，义为「被主张的」

definition_zh: 反方论点；针对某一主张提出的反对论证；文章或辩论中先摆出的对立观点
definition_en: an argument that opposes or challenges another argument, often presented before it is answered
core_image: 两个人对坐，桌上一张纸写着主张，另一张纸从对面推过来，写着相反的推论
scene: 论文写到第三段，作者先把可能反对自己的一方意见完整摆出来，再准备逐条回应。The essay admits a strong counterargument before defending its thesis.
sceneCN: 这里指先摆出来的对立观点（第 1 个义项：反对某一主张的论证）；句意为这篇文章在为自己的论点辩护之前，先承认一个强有力的反方论点。

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语「使清楚、证明」而来的名词，义为「论证；论点」
同源动词，义为「论证；争辩」
由名词加形容词尾构成，义为「好争辩的；论证性的」
由拉丁语「反对」而来的前缀，义为「反；对应」
由同一前缀加「主张」构成，义为「反诉；相反主张」

senses.title: An argument that opposes a thesis
senses.definition: a set of reasons put forward to show that another argument or claim is wrong or weak
senses.definitionCN: 为表明另一论证或主张有误或站不住而提出的一组理由
senses.example: The strongest counterargument is that the sample was too small.
senses.exampleCN: 最强的反方论点是样本太小。
senses.why: Counter- adds opposition to argument, so the word names the other side of a contested claim.
senses.whyCN: 前缀给「论证」加上对立，因此这个词指有争议主张的另一面。

senses.title: The opposing case in a debate
senses.definition: the body of argument that the opposing team or speaker presents
senses.definitionCN: 对方队伍或发言人提出的整套论证
senses.example: The negative team built its counterargument around cost.
senses.exampleCN: 反方队伍围绕成本构建了它的对立论证。
senses.why: Debate is organised into sides, and each side's case is literally an argument set against the other.
senses.whyCN: 辩论分成正反两方，每一方的立论就是对着另一方摆出的论证。

senses.title: The fairness paragraph of an essay
senses.titleCN: 文章中体现公允的段落
senses.definition: the part of an essay that states the opposing view before answering it
senses.definitionCN: 文章在回应之前先陈述对立观点的部分
senses.example: A short counterargument paragraph makes the paper look fair.
senses.exampleCN: 一段简短的反方论点使文章显得公允。
senses.why: Academic writing treats the opposing view as a required move, so the word also names that paragraph.
senses.whyCN: 学术写作把对立观点当作必要的一步，因此这个词也指那一段。

senses.title: A rival explanation in research
senses.definition: an alternative explanation that could account for the same observations
senses.definitionCN: 能对同一批观察给出解释的另一种说法
senses.example: The authors tested a counterargument based on weather rather than policy.
senses.exampleCN: 作者检验了一个基于天气而非政策提出的竞争性解释。
senses.why: In science the opponent is not a person but another explanation, and it must be ruled out.
senses.whyCN: 在科学里，对手不是人而是另一种解释，它必须被排除。

senses.title: A hypothetical objection used as a test
senses.titleCN: 用作检验的假想反对意见
senses.definition: an objection thought up to stress-test a claim before it is published
senses.definitionCN: 在发表之前用来压力测试某一主张而想出的反对意见
senses.example: She wrote the strongest counterargument she could imagine.
senses.exampleCN: 她写下了自己能想到的最强反方论点。
senses.why: Imagining the opposition is a method, since a claim that survives a hard objection is stronger.
senses.whyCN: 想象反对意见是一种方法，经得住严厉质疑的主张更稳固。

senses.title: The opposing legal case
senses.definition: the version of facts and law that the opposing party argues in a dispute
senses.definitionCN: 争议中对方当事人所主张的事实与法律版本
senses.example: Counsel spent the morning preparing a counterargument on jurisdiction.
senses.exampleCN: 律师整个上午都在准备关于管辖权的反方论证。
senses.why: Litigation is an argument with consequences, and each party's case is a counterargument to the other's.
senses.whyCN: 诉讼是带后果的论证，每一方的主张都是对另一方主张的反论。

senses.title: A challenge to a policy
senses.definition: a reasoned objection to a proposed measure or official plan
senses.definitionCN: 对拟议措施或官方计划提出的有理有据的反对
senses.example: The committee heard a counterargument from the small firms.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会听取了小企业提出的反方论证。
senses.why: Policy debate reproduces the academic form, with objections stated before decisions are taken.
senses.whyCN: 政策辩论复制了学术的形式：在作出决定前先陈述反对意见。

senses.title: A move that shows balance
senses.definition: the rhetorical act of presenting the other view so that one's own case appears measured
senses.definitionCN: 先呈现对方观点、使自己的立场显得持中的修辞动作
senses.example: The speaker opened with a counterargument to win the audience's trust.
senses.exampleCN: 发言者先抛出一个反方论点来赢得听众信任。
senses.why: Stating the other side first is a way of borrowing its credibility, which is why the move is taught explicitly.
senses.whyCN: 先讲对方一面是借取其公信力的办法，所以这一招被明确写进写作教材。

intro.en: Counterargument is a transparent compound: a Latin prefix meaning against joined to a Latin word for a reasoned argument. The word names the opposing case itself, not the answer to it.
intro.cn: 这是一个构词透明的组合：表示「反对」的拉丁前缀，加上表示「有理据的论证」的拉丁词。它指对立方的主张本身，而不是对它的回应。

items.en: Contra meant against or opposite, and it survives in English prefixes and in words such as contradict.
items.cn: 这个词意为「反对、相对」，至今保存在英语前缀以及「反驳」一类词里。

items.en: Arguere meant to make clear, to prove, and also to accuse; the proving sense fed the modern word for argument.
items.cn: 这个词意为「使清楚、证明」，也指指控；其中「证明」义喂养了现代的「论证」一词。

items.en: Argumentum named the content of a proof, and English took argument through French with the same core.
items.cn: 这个词指证明的内容，英语经法语引入「论证」，核心义相同。

items.en: Old French used contre- for opposition in compounds, and English borrowed the pattern.
items.cn: 古法语用这一前缀表示复合词中的对立，英语借用了这种构词方式。

items.en: The compound appeared in English in the nineteenth century; the exact first record is uncertain.
items.cn: 这个复合词在十九世纪的英语中出现；确切的最早记录不确定。

items.en: Composition teaching fixed counterargument as the paragraph that states the other view, making it a classroom term.
items.cn: 写作教学把「反方论点」固定为陈述对方观点的那一段，使它成为课堂术语。

note.en: The first group shares the argument root or the opposition prefix; the second group names the answer rather than the opposing case.
note.cn: 第一组共享「论证」词根或「反对」前缀；第二组指回应，而不是对立方的主张。

entries.definition: A set of reasons offered in support of a position.
entries.definitionCN: 指为某一立场提供的一组理由。

entries.definition: To give reasons for or against something.
entries.definitionCN: 指为或反对某事给出理由。

entries.definition: A claim set against another claim, often in law.
entries.definitionCN: 指对着另一主张提出的主张，常用于法律。

entries.definition: A contrasting element; its root is a point, not an argument.
entries.definitionCN: 指形成对照的要素；词根是「点」，不是「论证」。

entries.definition: A case that disproves a general statement.
entries.definitionCN: 指推翻一般性陈述的反例。

entries.definition: To meet unexpectedly; it looks like counter but comes from a meeting prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 指意外相遇；形似却来自表示相遇的前缀。

entries.definition: The answer that tries to disprove the opposing argument, not the opposing argument itself.
entries.definitionCN: 指试图驳倒对方论证的回应，而不是对方论证本身。

entries.definition: A stated reason for opposing something, often shorter than a full argument.
entries.definitionCN: 指反对某事的理由，通常比完整论证短。

entries.definition: The act of proving an argument false.
entries.definitionCN: 指证明某论证为假的行为。

entries.definition: The position held by those who disagree, stated without the full reasoning.
entries.definitionCN: 指不同意者的立场，未必带完整推理。

entries.definition: A call to justify a claim, weaker than a worked-out argument.
entries.definitionCN: 指要求为某主张给出理由，比完整论证弱。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the two papers facing each other, the essay paragraph and the debate side.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用两张对推的纸、作文里的那一段与辩论中的一方。

normal.en: Counter means against and argument means reasons, so the word is simply the reasons against.
normal.cn: 前缀意为「反对」，后一半意为「理由」，所以这个词就是「反对的理由」。

normal.en: The essay phrase is «acknowledge the counterargument», a standard move in composition.
normal.cn: 作文里的固定说法是「承认反方论点」，是写作中的标准动作。

normal.en: A counterargument is not a rebuttal: one is the punch, the other is the block.
normal.cn: 反方论点不是反驳：一个是打出的拳，一个是挡回的格。

normal.en: A counterexample is a single case; a counterargument is a whole case against you.
normal.cn: 反例是一个事例，反方论点则是整套反对你的理由。

normal.en: In debate the negative team's whole case can be called the counterargument.
normal.cn: 在辩论中，反方队伍的整体立论可称为反方论点。

abstract.en: A counterargument is the shadow that proves the light exists, since a claim with no opposition is not yet a claim.
abstract.cn: 反方论点是证明光存在的影子，因为无人反对的主张还称不上主张。

abstract.en: Arguing against yourself is the cheapest way to find out what you actually believe.
abstract.cn: 与自己争辩，是弄清自己真正相信什么的最省力的办法。

abstract.en: Every strong case carries its opponent inside it from the beginning.
abstract.cn: 每个强立论从一开始就把对手装在自己体内。

examples.en: The paper addresses the main counterargument in a single paragraph.
examples.cn: 这篇论文用一段回应了主要的反方论点。

examples.en: Ignoring a counterargument makes a proposal look weak.
examples.cn: 忽视反方论点会让提案显得薄弱。

examples.en: She offered a counterargument based on the cost of the scheme.
examples.cn: 她基于该方案的成本提出了一个反方论点。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「反」加「论证」：对着你的主张推回来的那套理由，就是反方论点

root: 前缀来自拉丁语 contra「反对、相对」；后一半来自拉丁语 argumentum「证明的内容」，其动词 arguere 意为「使清楚、证明」。古法语用对立前缀构词，英语借用；复合词在十九世纪出现，写作教学在二十世纪把它固定为「陈述对方观点的那一段」。最早记录年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses run from the claim to the classroom: an opposing argument, a debate side, the fairness paragraph, a rival explanation, a hypothetical test, the legal case, a policy challenge, and a balancing move.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从主张延伸到课堂：反对论证、辩论一方、公允段落、竞争性解释、假想检验、法律主张、政策质疑、平衡姿态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two sheets of paper travel toward each other across a table, each carrying reasons against the other.
core.cn: 核心意象：两张纸在桌面上相互推近，各自写着反对对方的理由。

branches.en: THE OPPOSING CASE: reasons set against a claim, whether in writing or in debate.
branches.cn: 对立的主张：对着某一论点摆出的理由，无论书面还是辩论。

branches.en: THE FAIRNESS MOVE: stating the other view first so one's own case looks measured.
branches.cn: 公允之举：先讲对方观点，使自己的立场显得持中。

branches.en: THE RIVAL EXPLANATION: another account of the same facts, waiting to be ruled out.
branches.cn: 竞争性解释：对同一批事实的另一说法，等着被排除。

branches.en: THE SELF-TEST: an objection invented to try to break one's own claim.
branches.cn: 自我检验：为击破自身主张而想出的反对意见。

branches.en: THE OUTSIDE ARENA: the legal case and the policy objection.
branches.cn: 外部场域：法律上的对方主张与政策质疑。

intro.en: Counterargument is a compound of a Latin opposition prefix and a Latin argument word, and neither half has changed meaning.
intro.cn: 这个词组由拉丁语的对立前缀与论证词构成，两半的含义都没有改变。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies contra and argumentum; English supplies the combining habit that made them one word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了「反对」与「论证」，英语提供了把它们合成一个词的构词习惯。

items.example: It marks the opposing side of a claim.
items.exampleCN: 它标出主张的对立一面。

items.example: The root of the argument family.
items.exampleCN: 这是「论证」一族的词根。

items.example: It became English argument.
items.exampleCN: 它成为英语的「论证」。

items.example: It forms the compound with argument.
items.exampleCN: 它与「论证」合成这个复合词。

items.meaning: the result or means of an action
items.example: It marks the noun argument.
items.exampleCN: 它标出名词「论证」。

items.example: The same pattern applied to law.
items.exampleCN: 同一构词方式用于法律。

items.meaning: a case against a general claim
items.example: The same prefix applied to a case.
items.exampleCN: 同一前缀用于「事例」。

items.example: It is the response, not the opposing case.
items.exampleCN: 它是回应，而非对方主张。

derivatives.zh: 拉丁「证明的内容」经法语而来，义为「论证；论点」
同源动词，义为「论证；争辩」
加形容词尾，义为「好争辩的」
同前缀复合，义为「反诉；相反主张」
同前缀复合，义为「反例」

definition_zh: 反驳；对指责或论点作出的驳斥；辩论中的反驳发言；法律上提出的反证
definition_en: a reply that answers an accusation or argument and tries to disprove it
core_image: 一只手把对方推过来的石块原样顶回去，石块落地，桌面重新空出来
scene: 对方刚说完质疑，发言人没有回避，而是拿出两份记录逐条把质疑顶了回去。Her rebuttal used the same data to reach the opposite conclusion.
sceneCN: 这里指用证据把对方质疑驳回去的回应（第 1 个义项：驳斥对方论点的回应）；句意为她的反驳用同一批数据得出了相反的结论。

derivatives.zh: 由同一法语词干构成的动词，义为「反驳；驳斥」
加已然词尾，义为「已被驳斥的」
加表示「可……的」形容词尾，义为「可反驳的」
加施动者名词尾，义为「反驳者；法律上的答辩」
加行为名词尾，义为「反驳动作」

senses.title: A reply that disproves an argument
senses.definition: an answer that gives reasons or evidence showing an argument to be wrong
senses.definitionCN: 给出理由或证据、表明对方论证有误的回应
senses.example: Her rebuttal showed that the earlier figure had been misread.
senses.exampleCN: 她的反驳表明先前那个数字被误读了。
senses.why: The French verb meant to push back, and a rebuttal is exactly the push that returns an attack.
senses.whyCN: 这个法语动词意为「推回」，而反驳正是把攻击推回去的那一推。

senses.title: A speech answering the opponent
senses.definition: the speech in a debate that replies to the other side's case
senses.definitionCN: 辩论中回应对方立论的发言
senses.example: The third speaker delivered the rebuttal in four minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 第三位辩手用四分钟完成了反驳。
senses.why: Debate assigns a slot for the reply, so the word also names that turn at the microphone.
senses.whyCN: 辩论为回应留出一个环节，这个词也指麦克风前的那一轮。

senses.title: Contrary evidence in law
senses.definition: evidence offered to contradict evidence already presented by the other party
senses.definitionCN: 用来推翻对方已提交证据的证据
senses.example: The defence called a witness in rebuttal.
senses.exampleCN: 辩方传唤了一名证人作反证。
senses.why: Courts stage proof and counter-proof, and the counter-proof is literally evidence that pushes back.
senses.whyCN: 法庭上安排证明与反证明，反证明就是字面上把对方推回去的证据。

senses.title: A formal reply to criticism
senses.definition: an official written or spoken answer to public criticism
senses.definitionCN: 对公开批评作出的正式书面或口头答复
senses.example: The agency issued a detailed rebuttal of the audit.
senses.exampleCN: 该机构发布了一份对审计报告的详细反驳。
senses.why: Institutions must answer charges on the record, and that answer is a rebuttal rather than a denial.
senses.whyCN: 机构必须公开回应指控，而这种回应是逐条驳斥，不是一句否认。

senses.title: The section after a counterargument
senses.definition: the part of an essay that answers the opposing view it has just stated
senses.definitionCN: 文章中回应刚刚陈述的对立观点的部分
senses.example: The rebuttal occupies two paragraphs and cites three studies.
senses.exampleCN: 反驳部分占两段，引用了三项研究。
senses.why: Composition teaching pairs the opposing paragraph with an answering paragraph, and this is its name.
senses.whyCN: 写作教学把陈述对方的一段与回应的一段配对，这一段就叫反驳。

senses.title: A data-based refutation
senses.definition: a refutation that rests on measurements or records rather than on rhetoric
senses.definitionCN: 依靠测量或记录而非修辞的驳斥
senses.example: The rebuttal relied on the raw logs, not on the summary table.
senses.exampleCN: 这次反驳依靠原始日志，而不是汇总表。
senses.why: Numbers can push back too, and when they do the word keeps its physical picture.
senses.whyCN: 数字也能推回去，数字一推，这个词就保留着它的物理画面。

senses.title: A quick answer under pressure
senses.definition: an immediate verbal answer to a challenge in an interview or press conference
senses.definitionCN: 在采访或记者会上对质疑的即时口头回应
senses.example: His rebuttal came before the question had finished.
senses.exampleCN: 问题还没问完，他的反驳就来了。
senses.why: The word covers fast replies as well as polished ones, since pushing back needs no rehearsal.
senses.whyCN: 这个词既指打磨过的回应，也指快速回应，因为推回去不需要排练。

senses.title: An answer to a presumption
senses.definition: a legal answer that defeats a presumption the law would otherwise accept
senses.definitionCN: 推翻法律原本会接受的推定所做的答辩
senses.example: The filing offered a rebuttal of the presumption of regularity.
senses.exampleCN: 该文件对「合规推定」提出了抗辩。
senses.why: Law assumes some facts until challenged, and the challenge itself is called a rebuttal.
senses.whyCN: 法律先假定某些事实，直到有人质疑，而这个质疑本身就叫抗辩。

intro.en: Rebuttal comes from Old French rebouter, to push back, built from re- and a verb meaning to thrust. The English noun keeps the physical picture: an argument is struck, and the answer strikes it back.
intro.cn: 这个词来自古法语 rebouter「推回去」，由表示「回」的前缀与意为「顶、推」的动词构成。英语名词保留了物理画面：论证打过来，回应把它顶回去。

items.en: The thrusting verb behind Old French is reconstructed from Frankish; no written form survives, so its exact shape is uncertain.
items.cn: 古法语中表示「顶、推」的动词由法兰克语重构而来；没有书面形式留存，确切形态不确定。

items.en: This verb meant to thrust or push, and it also stands behind the English word butt, to push with the head.
items.cn: 这个动词意为顶、推，英语中表示以头顶撞的词也出自它。

items.en: With the prefix meaning back, the verb meant to repel or drive back an attack.
items.cn: 加上表示「回」的前缀后，动词意为击退、把攻击顶回去。

items.en: English took the verb through law and used it for answering a charge; the first record is approximate.
items.cn: 英语经法律用语引入这个动词，用于回应指控；最早记录为约数。

items.en: The action noun settled into English later and became the standard word for a debate reply.
items.cn: 动作名词较晚在英语中定型，成为辩论回应的标准说法。

items.en: Courts use it for contrary evidence, and composition teaching uses it for the paragraph that answers the opposing view.
items.cn: 法庭用它指反证，写作教学用它指回应对方观点的那一段。

note.en: The first group shares the pushing root or looks close; the second group names the opposing case or a plain denial.
note.cn: 第一组共享「推」词根或形近；第二组指对立方的主张或单纯的否认。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to drive back an argument or charge.
entries.definitionCN: 指把论证或指控顶回去的动词。

entries.definition: The past participle, used for a claim that has been answered.
entries.definitionCN: 过去分词，指已被回应的主张。

entries.definition: Able to be disproved, a common legal adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 指可被推翻的，是常用法律形容词。

entries.definition: A partial refund; its prefix means back but its root means to beat down in price.
entries.definitionCN: 指部分退款；前缀同表「回」，但词根指压价，属另一来源。

entries.definition: To rise against authority; it comes from a word for war, not for pushing.
entries.definitionCN: 指反抗权威；来自表示战争的词，与「推」无关。

entries.definition: To push with the head; the same thrusting verb survives separately.
entries.definitionCN: 指以头顶撞；同一个「顶」动词单独留存下来。

entries.definition: The opposing argument itself, not the reply that defeats it.
entries.definitionCN: 指对立的论证本身，而不是驳倒它的回应。

entries.definition: Proof that a statement is false, often more formal than a rebuttal.
entries.definitionCN: 指证明某陈述为假，通常比反驳更正式。

entries.definition: A statement that something is not true, without the supporting case.
entries.definitionCN: 指声称某事不实，但不带支撑性论证。

entries.definition: A reply, especially one that answers a reply.
entries.definitionCN: 指回应，尤指对回应的再回应。

entries.definition: The neutral word for any answer.
entries.definitionCN: 指任何回应的中性说法。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the pushed-back stone, the debate slot and the legal counter-proof.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用被顶回去的石块、辩论环节与法律反证。

normal.en: To rebut is to push back, and a rebuttal is the push itself.
normal.cn: 反驳就是推回去，而「反驳」这个名词就是那一推。

normal.en: The debate phrase is «deliver the rebuttal», a fixed turn in the format.
normal.cn: 辩论中的固定说法是「作反驳」，是赛制里的固定一轮。

normal.en: Rebuttal evidence is the legal phrase for proof that answers proof.
normal.cn: 「反证」是回应证据的证据在法律上的固定说法。

normal.en: A rebuttal comes after a counterargument: first the punch, then the block.
normal.cn: 反驳跟在反方论点之后：先出拳，再格挡。

normal.en: Rebuttal and refutation differ in tone: the first answers in the room, the second proves on paper.
normal.cn: 反驳与驳斥语气不同：前者在场上回应，后者在纸面上证明。

abstract.en: A rebuttal is an argument's immune response: it recognises the foreign claim and expels it.
abstract.cn: 反驳是论证的免疫反应：识别外来主张，再把它排出去。

abstract.en: Pushing back is not the same as refusing; the hand moves, and that movement is the answer.
abstract.cn: 推回去不等于拒之门外；手动了，这一动就是回答。

abstract.en: Whoever answers last sounds right, which is why rebuttal has a fixed place in debate.
abstract.cn: 最后说话的人听起来总有理，所以反驳在辩论里有固定位置。

examples.en: The minister's rebuttal was shorter than the report it answered.
examples.cn: 部长的反驳比它所回应的报告还短。

examples.en: She wrote a point-by-point rebuttal of the reviewer's comments.
examples.cn: 她针对审稿人的意见写了逐条反驳。

examples.en: The defence called two witnesses in rebuttal.
examples.cn: 辩方传唤了两名证人作反证。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「瑞巴投」——把对方扔来的球「投」回「瑞」气，就是反驳

root: 古法语 rebouter「推回去」= re-「回」+ 表示顶、推的动词，其更早的法兰克语形式属重构，确切形态不确定。英语十四世纪经法律用语引入动词，十九世纪名词定型为辩论与写作中的「反驳」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses run from the courtroom to the press room: disproving a reply, a debate speech, contrary evidence, an answer to criticism, an essay section, a data-based refutation, a quick answer, and a legal answer to a presumption.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从法庭延伸到记者会：驳倒回应、辩论发言、反证、对批评的答复、文章段落、数据驳斥、即时回应、对推定的抗辩。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stone thrown at a table is met by a hand that sends it straight back.
core.cn: 核心意象：掷向桌面的石块被一只手接住，又原样顶了回去。

branches.en: THE PUSHED REPLY: an answer that drives an attack back, whether polished or instant.
branches.cn: 顶回去的回应：把攻击送回的回答，无论打磨过还是即时的。

branches.en: THE DEBATE SLOT: the turn at the microphone reserved for answering the other side.
branches.cn: 辩论环节：为回应对方而保留的发言轮次。

branches.en: THE LEGAL COUNTER-PROOF: evidence against evidence, and an answer to a legal presumption.
branches.cn: 法律反证：对着证据的证据，以及对法律推定的抗辩。

branches.en: THE PUBLIC ANSWER: an institution's formal response to criticism.
branches.cn: 公开答复：机构对批评的正式回应。

branches.en: THE WRITTEN ANSWER: the essay section and the refutation built on data.
branches.cn: 书面回应：文章段落与以数据为依据的驳斥。

intro.en: Rebuttal comes from a French verb of pushing back, and its root survives in the English word for butting with the head.
intro.cn: 这个词来自法语的「推回」动词，其词根还留在英语中表示以头顶撞的词里。

latinIntro.en: The deeper root is reconstructed, so only the French stages can be cited with confidence.
latinIntro.cn: 更早的词根属重构，只能有把握地引用法语各阶段。

items.example: It turns thrusting into thrusting back.
items.exampleCN: 它把「顶」变成「顶回去」。

items.example: The pushing half of the word.
items.exampleCN: 这是词里「推」的那一半。

items.example: The direct source of English rebut.
items.exampleCN: 这是英语「反驳」动词的直接来源。

items.example: It forms rebuttal from the verb stem.
items.exampleCN: 它由动词词干构成名词「反驳」。

items.example: It forms rebuttable.
items.exampleCN: 它构成「可反驳的」。

items.example: It forms rebutter.
items.exampleCN: 它构成「反驳者」。

items.example: It forms the adjective rebutted.
items.exampleCN: 它构成形容词「已被驳斥的」。

items.example: The English verb that the noun is built from.
items.exampleCN: 这是名词所依托的英语动词。
