definition_zh: 支持性证据；用来撑住某一主张或结论的证据材料
definition_en: evidence offered to back up a claim or conclusion
core_image: 一根细柱撑在倾斜的屋檐下，屋檐不再下沉，柱子本身却不起眼
scene: 报告写到结论一段，作者把三份问卷结果依次列出，用来撑住前面的判断。The lawyer presented supporting evidence for each element of the claim.
sceneCN: 这里指用来支撑主张的证据（第 1 个义项：支撑某一结论的材料）；句意为律师为该主张的每个要件都提交了支持性证据。

pos.zh: 支持性证据；支撑材料（不可数）

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语「从下搬运」而来的动词，义为「支撑；支持」
由动词加形容词尾构成，义为「给予支持的」
加施动者名词尾，义为「支持者」
加已然词尾，义为「得到支持的」
由拉丁语「明显可见」而来的名词，义为「证据」
同源形容词，义为「明显的」
加形容词尾，义为「证据性的」

senses.title: Evidence that holds up a claim
senses.definition: material offered in order to keep a claim from collapsing under doubt
senses.definitionCN: 为使主张不在质疑下垮掉而提供的材料
senses.example: The report offers supporting evidence for every one of its forecasts.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告为其中每一项预测都提供了支持性证据。
senses.why: Support means to carry weight from below, and evidence that supports does exactly that for a claim.
senses.whyCN: 「支撑」指从下面承重，支持性证据对主张做的正是这件事。

senses.title: Data cited inside an argument
senses.definition: figures or records quoted at the point where an argument needs them
senses.definitionCN: 在论证需要之处被引用的数字或记录
senses.example: Each paragraph pairs a claim with supporting evidence.
senses.exampleCN: 每一段都把主张与支持性证据配在一起。
senses.why: An argument has joints, and data placed at those joints keeps the reasoning from separating.
senses.whyCN: 论证有接缝，放在接缝处的数据能防止推理散开。

senses.title: Documents that corroborate a record
senses.definition: papers that confirm the accuracy of an existing record or account
senses.definitionCN: 用来确认已有记录或说法准确性的文件
senses.example: Auditors asked for supporting evidence behind the invoice.
senses.exampleCN: 审计人员要求提供发票背后的支持性文件。
senses.why: A record alone is a statement; a document that backs it turns the statement into something checked.
senses.whyCN: 记录本身只是说法，撑住它的文件把这个说法变成经过核对的东西。

senses.title: Examples used as illustration
senses.definition: instances chosen to show that a general claim actually occurs
senses.definitionCN: 为表明某一一般性主张确实发生而选取的事例
senses.example: The lecturer used three case studies as supporting evidence.
senses.exampleCN: 讲师用三个案例作为支持性证据。
senses.why: An example is a small piece of the world that fits the claim, so it can carry part of the weight.
senses.whyCN: 例子是世界中契合该主张的一小块，因此能承担一部分重量。

senses.title: Statistical results backing a hypothesis
senses.definition: test results or estimates that make a hypothesis more credible
senses.definitionCN: 使某一假设更可信的检验结果或估计值
senses.example: The correlation was offered as supporting evidence for the theory.
senses.exampleCN: 这一相关性被作为该理论的支持性证据提出。
senses.why: Statistics compress many observations into one number, and that number can stand under a hypothesis.
senses.whyCN: 统计把许多观察压缩成一个数字，这个数字就能站在假设下面。

senses.title: Testimony in a legal case
senses.definition: witness statements used to uphold a party's version of events
senses.definitionCN: 用来支撑一方事实版本的证人陈述
senses.example: Her testimony was the only supporting evidence for the alibi.
senses.exampleCN: 她的证言是该不在场证明唯一的支持性证据。
senses.why: Courts weigh stories against stories, and testimony is the human form of support.
senses.whyCN: 法庭让不同说法互相比重，证言是「支撑」的人格化形式。

senses.title: Earlier studies cited in a review
senses.titleCN: 综述中引用的既有研究
senses.definition: published findings from other researchers used to back a statement
senses.definitionCN: 用来支撑某一陈述的其他研究者已发表的结果
senses.example: The review lists supporting evidence from twelve countries.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇综述列出了来自十二个国家的支持性证据。
senses.why: Science builds on what is already published, so earlier papers are beams borrowed from other buildings.
senses.whyCN: 科学建立在已发表的内容上，因此早先的论文是从别的建筑借来的梁。

senses.title: Material that raises confidence
senses.definition: anything that makes an audience more willing to accept a claim
senses.definitionCN: 使读者或听众更愿意接受某一主张的任何材料
senses.example: A single graph served as supporting evidence for the whole plan.
senses.exampleCN: 一张图就充当了整个方案的支持性证据。
senses.why: The phrase describes a function rather than a kind, so almost any material can play this role.
senses.whyCN: 这个词组描述的是功能而非类别，所以几乎任何材料都能扮演这个角色。

intro.en: Supporting evidence joins a Latin verb meaning to carry from below to a Latin noun meaning clearness. Something is carried under a claim so that the claim can stand.
intro.cn: 这个词组把拉丁语中表示「从下面搬运」的动词，与表示「明显」的名词接在一起：把东西搬到主张下面，主张才立得住。

items.en: Portare meant to carry, and it stands behind transport, portable and report.
items.cn: 这个词根意为「搬运」，英语中「运输」「便携」「报告」等词都出自它。

items.en: With the prefix meaning from below, the verb meant to carry or hold up, hence to bear a weight.
items.cn: 加上表示「从下」的前缀后，动词意为托住、撑起，因而指承重。

items.en: English support appeared in the fourteenth century for holding something up, then for backing a person or claim.
items.cn: 英语的「支撑」在十四世纪出现，先指托住实物，后指支持某人或主张。

items.en: Videre meant to see, and its compound with the prefix for out produced evident, what can be seen clearly.
items.cn: 这个词根意为「看」，与表示「向外」的前缀复合后产生「明显的」，即看得清楚。

items.en: Evidentia named clearness itself, and English evidence came to mean the material that makes a fact clear.
items.cn: 这个词指「清楚」本身，英语的「证据」遂指使事实清楚的材料。

items.en: The two words were fixed together in legal and academic writing; the exact first record of the phrase is uncertain.
items.cn: 这两个词在法律与学术写作中被固定组合；确切的最早记录不确定。

note.en: The first group belongs to the support or evidence families; the second group names other kinds of proof.
note.cn: 第一组属于「支撑」或「证据」同族；第二组指其他类型的证明。

entries.definition: To hold up or back something with weight or approval.
entries.definitionCN: 指以承重或赞成来托住某物。

entries.definition: Giving help or encouragement rather than weight.
entries.definitionCN: 指给予帮助或鼓励，而非承重。

entries.definition: A person who backs a team, cause or person.
entries.definitionCN: 指支持某队、某事业或某人的人。

entries.definition: Material that tends to establish a fact.
entries.definitionCN: 指倾向于确立某事实的材料。

entries.definition: Plainly seen or understood.
entries.definitionCN: 指清楚可见或易懂的。

entries.definition: As the facts plainly show.
entries.definitionCN: 指从事实清楚地看。

entries.definition: Evidence from observation or experiment, defined by its source rather than its role.
entries.definitionCN: 指来自观察或实验的证据，按来源而非作用界定。

entries.definition: Evidence that confirms a statement already made by another source.
entries.definitionCN: 指确认另一来源已作出陈述的证据。

entries.definition: Indirect evidence from which a fact may be inferred.
entries.definitionCN: 指可从中推断事实的间接证据。

entries.definition: Evidence strong enough to settle a question.
entries.definitionCN: 指强到足以了结问题的证据。

entries.definition: Records that support a claim or process.
entries.definitionCN: 指支撑主张或流程的记录。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the pillar under an eave and the real pairing of a claim with its material.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用屋檐下的柱子，以及主张与材料之间的真实配对。

normal.en: Support is a pillar, and supporting evidence is the pillar under a sentence.
normal.cn: 支撑是一根柱子，支持性证据就是句子下面的那根柱子。

normal.en: Every claim in a good report has its own supporting evidence attached.
normal.cn: 好报告里的每个主张都附有自己的支持性证据。

normal.en: The legal phrase is «supporting evidence for the claim», used element by element.
normal.cn: 法律上的固定说法是「为该主张提供支持性证据」，逐个要件使用。

normal.en: Evidence comes from a word for clearness, so evidence is what makes a fact visible.
normal.cn: 「证据」来自表示「清楚」的词，所以证据就是让事实可见的东西。

normal.en: A supporting example carries less weight than a supporting measurement, but it still carries some.
normal.cn: 支持性的例子比支持性的测量轻，但仍承担一部分重量。

abstract.en: Support is silent work: nobody notices the pillar until the roof moves.
abstract.cn: 支撑是无声的工作：屋顶不动，就没人注意柱子。

abstract.en: A claim chooses its evidence the way a building chooses its beams, and weak choices show under load.
abstract.cn: 主张选择证据如同建筑选择梁，弱选择在承重时才显形。

abstract.en: The same fact can support opposite claims, which is why the beam must be inspected, not just counted.
abstract.cn: 同一事实能支撑相反主张，所以梁要检验，而不只是计数。

examples.en: The chapter provides supporting evidence for each of the three conclusions.
examples.cn: 这一章为三项结论中的每一项都提供了支持性证据。

examples.en: Without supporting evidence, the recommendation reads as an opinion.
examples.cn: 没有支持性证据，这项建议读起来就像个人意见。

examples.en: The auditor found no supporting evidence for the reported savings.
examples.cn: 审计人员没有找到支持所报节省额的支持性证据。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「支持」是柱子，「证据」是材料：柱子顶住主张，材料撑住柱子，就是支持性证据

root: 「支持」来自拉丁语 supportare「从下搬运、托住」，由 sub-「在下」与 portare「搬运」构成；「证据」来自拉丁语 evidentia「清楚」，由 ex-「向外」与 videre「看」构成。两词在法律与学术写作中被固定组合；该短语最早记录不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses run from the pillar to the courtroom: evidence holding a claim, data in an argument, corroborating papers, illustrative examples, statistical results, testimony, earlier studies, and any material that raises confidence.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从柱子延伸到法庭：撑住主张的证据、论证中的数据、佐证文件、说明性例子、统计结果、证言、既有研究、任何提高可信度的材料。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a slim post is placed under a sagging eave, and the roof stops moving.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根细柱被支在下沉的屋檐下，屋顶不再移动。

branches.en: THE LOAD PATH: material placed under a claim so that the claim can stand.
branches.cn: 承重路径：放在主张下面的材料，使主张立得住。

branches.en: THE CHECKED RECORD: documents that confirm an existing account.
branches.cn: 被核对的记录：确认已有说法的文件。

branches.en: THE SMALLER SUPPORTS: examples and statistical results that carry part of the weight.
branches.cn: 较小的支撑：承担部分重量的例子与统计结果。

branches.en: THE HUMAN AND PUBLISHED BEAMS: testimony and earlier studies.
branches.cn: 人与已发表之梁：证言与既有研究。

branches.en: THE FUNCTIONAL ROLE: anything that makes a claim easier to accept.
branches.cn: 功能角色：任何使主张更易被接受的东西。

intro.en: The phrase joins a Latin carrying verb to a Latin clearness noun, and both halves still describe physical action and visibility.
intro.cn: 这个词组把拉丁语的搬运动词与「清楚」名词接起来，两半至今都描述物理动作与可见性。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies supportare and evidentia; the English participles and endings are native additions.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了「托住」与「清楚」；英语的分词与词尾是本族添加。

items.example: It makes the carrying into bearing from below.
items.exampleCN: 它把「搬运」变成从下面托住。

items.example: The root of transport and report.
items.exampleCN: 这是「运输」与「报告」的词根。

items.example: The direct source of English support.
items.exampleCN: 这是英语「支撑」的直接来源。

items.example: It forms the adjective supporting.
items.exampleCN: 它构成形容词「支撑的」。

items.example: The root of evidence and vision.
items.exampleCN: 这是「证据」与「视觉」的词根。

items.example: It makes seeing into seeing clearly.
items.exampleCN: 它把「看」变成「看清」。

items.example: It became English evidence.
items.exampleCN: 它成为英语的「证据」。

items.example: It marks the noun evidence.
items.exampleCN: 它标出名词「证据」。

derivatives.zh: 拉丁「托住」经法语而来的动词，义为「支撑；支持」
加形容词尾，义为「给予支持的」
加施动者名词尾，义为「支持者」
拉丁「清楚」经法语而来的名词，义为「证据」
同源形容词，义为「明显的」
加形容词尾，义为「证据性的」

definition_zh: 实证证据；由观察、测量或实验得到、而非仅靠推理得出的证据
definition_en: evidence gained by observation, measurement or experiment rather than by reasoning alone
core_image: 田野外一本记录册摊开，页上是手写的观测数字，旁边的仪器还带着露水
scene: 论文的方法一节说明，结论不是从模型推出来的，而是从三百次实地测量中得来的。The claim is backed by empirical evidence from ten years of field records.
sceneCN: 这里指从实际观测中得来的证据（第 1 个义项：来自观察与测量的证据）；句意为该主张有十年野外记录形成的实证证据支撑。

derivatives.zh: 由希腊语「经验」经拉丁语而来的形容词，义为「实证的；经验的」
加副词尾，义为「以实证方式」
加表示主义的名词尾，义为「经验主义」
加表示从事者的名词尾，义为「经验论者」
同词干名词，义为「经验主义者；江湖医生（旧义）」

senses.title: Evidence from observation or experiment
senses.titleCN: 来自观察或实验的证据
senses.definition: material produced by watching, measuring or testing rather than by argument
senses.definitionCN: 通过观察、测量或试验产生、而非由论证产生的材料
senses.example: The theory has empirical evidence behind it at last.
senses.exampleCN: 这个理论终于有了实证证据支撑。
senses.why: Empirical names what rests on experience, and evidence from the senses is the form experience takes in research.
senses.whyCN: 「实证的」指建立在经验之上，而感官所得的证据就是经验在研究中的形态。

senses.title: Field data
senses.definition: records collected in the setting where the phenomenon actually occurs
senses.definitionCN: 在现象真实发生的场景中收集的记录
senses.example: The team spent two seasons gathering empirical evidence in the delta.
senses.exampleCN: 团队在三角洲花了两个季节收集实证证据。
senses.why: The field is where conditions are uncontrolled and therefore real, which is the point of this kind of evidence.
senses.whyCN: 野外条件不受控制因而真实，这正是这类证据的意义。

senses.title: Measurement results
senses.definition: readings taken with instruments under stated conditions
senses.definitionCN: 在规定条件下用仪器取得的读数
senses.example: The empirical evidence includes pressure readings taken every hour.
senses.exampleCN: 这些实证证据包括每小时记录的气压读数。
senses.why: A measurement is experience turned into a number, and numbers can be checked by others.
senses.whyCN: 测量是把经验变成数字，而数字可被他人核对。

senses.title: Clinical trial data
senses.definition: outcomes recorded from patients under a controlled treatment protocol
senses.definitionCN: 在受控治疗方案下记录的患者结果
senses.example: Regulators asked for empirical evidence from a randomised trial.
senses.exampleCN: 监管机构要求提供随机试验产生的实证证据。
senses.why: Medicine insists on evidence produced by treated bodies, since reasoning about the body is not enough.
senses.whyCN: 医学坚持采用由受治身体产生的证据，因为对身体仅作推理并不够。

senses.title: Survey data
senses.definition: responses collected systematically from a defined group of people
senses.definitionCN: 从界定人群系统收集的回答
senses.example: The survey supplied empirical evidence about household spending.
senses.exampleCN: 这项调查提供了关于家庭支出的实证证据。
senses.why: Asking many people the same question turns scattered experience into a dataset.
senses.whyCN: 向许多人问同一个问题，就把分散的经验变成数据集。

senses.title: Evidence that can be reproduced
senses.definition: findings that another team can obtain again by repeating the procedure
senses.definitionCN: 另一团队重做同一程序仍可得到的发现
senses.example: No empirical evidence survived the replication attempt.
senses.exampleCN: 没有任何实证证据经受住重复实验。
senses.why: Experience that only one person has is testimony, but experience that repeats becomes evidence.
senses.whyCN: 只有一人拥有的经验是证词，能够重复的经验才成为证据。

senses.title: Statistical evidence from samples
senses.definition: estimates and tests computed from a sample drawn from a larger population
senses.definitionCN: 从较大总体中抽取样本后计算出的估计与检验结果
senses.example: The empirical evidence came from a sample of four hundred firms.
senses.exampleCN: 这些实证证据来自四百家企业的样本。
senses.why: Sampling lets a small observed part speak for a whole that was never seen.
senses.whyCN: 抽样让被观察到的一小部分替从未被看见的整体说话。

senses.title: Evidence used to test, not illustrate
senses.titleCN: 用于检验而非说明的证据
senses.definition: observations brought in to challenge a theory rather than to decorate it
senses.definitionCN: 用来挑战理论、而非给理论作装饰的观察
senses.example: A good study seeks empirical evidence that could prove it wrong.
senses.exampleCN: 好的研究会去寻找能证明自己错了的实证证据。
senses.why: The strongest use of experience is the attempt to falsify, since a claim that cannot fail is not tested.
senses.whyCN: 经验最强的用法是试图证伪，因为不会失败的主张并未被检验。

intro.en: Empirical evidence joins a Greek word for experience, which entered English through Latin medicine, to a Latin word for clearness. The pair insists that what is seen and measured, not what is merely argued, makes a fact clear.
intro.cn: 这个词组把希腊语中表示「经验」的词（经拉丁语医学用语进入英语），与拉丁语中表示「清楚」的词接在一起：使事实清楚的是被看见与被测量的东西，而不是仅凭论证。

items.en: Peira meant a trial or attempt, and it stands behind the word for experience; its deeper origin is not established.
items.cn: 这个词意为「尝试、试验」，是「经验」一词的来源；它更早的来源尚未确立。

items.en: With the prefix meaning in, the noun meant experience gained by trying things, as against pure reasoning.
items.cn: 加上表示「在内」的前缀后，这个名词指通过尝试得到的经验，与纯推理相对。

items.en: Latin named the physician who worked from observed cases rather than from theory, and English empiric followed.
items.cn: 拉丁语用这个词指凭观察病例而非理论行医的医生，英语的「经验主义者」随之出现。

items.en: The adjective shifted to the neutral sense of based on observation, especially in natural philosophy.
items.cn: 这个形容词转向中性含义「以观察为基础的」，尤用于自然哲学。

items.en: Evidentia meant clearness, and evidence became the material that makes a fact clear to a observer.
items.cn: 这个词意为「清楚」，「证据」遂指使事实对观察者变得清楚的材料。

items.en: The two words were fixed together in nineteenth-century science writing; the exact first record of the phrase is uncertain.
items.cn: 这两个词在十九世纪的科学写作中被固定组合；该短语确切的最早记录不确定。

note.en: The first group belongs to the experience family or looks similar; the second group names evidence by its role or its strength.
note.cn: 第一组属于「经验」同族或形近；第二组按作用或强度给证据分类。

entries.definition: Based on observation or experiment rather than theory.
entries.definitionCN: 指以观察或实验而非理论为基础的。

entries.definition: In a way that rests on observed data.
entries.definitionCN: 指以依赖观测数据的方式。

entries.definition: The philosophical view that knowledge comes from experience.
entries.definitionCN: 指知识来自经验的哲学观点。

entries.definition: A person who holds that knowledge comes from experience.
entries.definitionCN: 指主张知识来自经验的人。

entries.definition: A group of territories under one ruler; it starts from a word for command, not experience.
entries.definitionCN: 指由一位统治者统辖的领土群；起首是表示命令的词，与经验无关。

entries.definition: Relating to an empire; the resemblance is only in sound.
entries.definitionCN: 指与帝国有关的；相似仅在读音。

entries.definition: Evidence from watching without intervening, a narrower source.
entries.definitionCN: 指不介入地观察所得的证据，来源更窄。

entries.definition: Evidence from deliberate manipulation and control.
entries.definitionCN: 指经有意操作与控制所得的证据。

entries.definition: Evidence expressed as numbers, whatever its source.
entries.definitionCN: 指以数字表达的证据，不论来源。

entries.definition: Evidence from personal stories, casual and unsystematic.
entries.definitionCN: 指来自个人讲述的证据，随意且不系统。

entries.definition: Reasoning from principles without observational support.
entries.definitionCN: 指由原理推出、没有观测支撑的推理。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the field notebook, the trial and measurement, and the test-not-illustrate role.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用野外记录册、试验与测量，以及「用于检验而非装饰」的作用。

normal.en: Empirical means from experience, so empirical evidence is what the senses and instruments report.
normal.cn: 「实证的」意为来自经验，所以实证证据就是感官与仪器报告的内容。

normal.en: Field records, trial data and survey answers are all real sources of this kind of evidence.
normal.cn: 野外记录、试验数据与调查回答都是这类证据的真实来源。

normal.en: Empirical is the adjective, empirically the adverb, empiricism the philosophy behind it.
normal.cn: 「实证的」是形容词，「以实证方式」是副词，「经验主义」是它背后的哲学。

normal.en: A randomised trial is the clearest case, because the comparison is built into the design.
normal.cn: 随机试验是最清楚的情形，因为比较被写进了设计。

normal.en: The strongest empirical work tries to find evidence that would defeat its own claim.
normal.cn: 最强的实证研究试图找到能击败自身主张的证据。

abstract.en: Experience is the world answering back, and empirical evidence is the record of that answer.
abstract.cn: 经验是世界在回话，实证证据就是那句回话的记录。

abstract.en: A theory that cannot be embarrassed by data is not really a theory but a belief.
abstract.cn: 不会被数据弄得难堪的理论，其实不是理论而是信念。

abstract.en: The field notebook is humble, yet it outranks the elegant model when the two disagree.
abstract.cn: 野外记录册很不起眼，可它一与漂亮模型冲突就压过模型。

examples.en: There is little empirical evidence that the policy changed behaviour.
examples.cn: 几乎没有实证证据表明该政策改变了行为。

examples.en: The argument is elegant but lacks empirical evidence.
examples.cn: 这个论证很漂亮，却缺少实证证据。

examples.en: They collected empirical evidence from forty schools over three years.
examples.cn: 他们用三年时间从四十所学校收集实证证据。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「实证」来自「经验」，「证据」来自「看清」：亲手试过、量过，把事实看清，就是实证证据

root: 「实证的」源自希腊语 empeiria「经验」，由 en-「在内」与 peira「尝试」构成，经拉丁语医学用语 empiricus 进入英语，十七世纪转为「以观察为基础」的中性义。「证据」来自拉丁语 evidentia「清楚」。该短语在十九世纪科学写作中固定；最早记录不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses run from the field to the test: observation, field data, measurements, trial data, survey data, reproducible findings, sample statistics, and evidence used to try to falsify.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从野外延伸到检验：观察、野外数据、测量、试验数据、调查数据、可重复的发现、样本统计、用于证伪的证据。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a notebook of hand-written readings lies open in a field, dew still on the instrument beside it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一本手写读数的记录册在野外摊开，旁边仪器上还挂着露水。

branches.en: THE OBSERVED WORLD: evidence taken from settings where the phenomenon is real.
branches.cn: 被观察的世界：从现象真实发生的场景取得的证据。

branches.en: THE INSTRUMENT AND THE TRIAL: readings and controlled patient outcomes.
branches.cn: 仪器与试验：读数与受控的患者结果。

branches.en: THE ASKED AND SAMPLED: survey answers and estimates from a sample.
branches.cn: 提问与抽样：调查回答与由样本得出的估计。

branches.en: THE REPEATABLE FINDING: a result another team can obtain again.
branches.cn: 可重复的发现：另一团队能再次得到的结果。

branches.en: THE FALSIFYING USE: observations brought in to defeat a claim.
branches.cn: 证伪的用法：用来击败主张的观察。

intro.en: The phrase joins a Greek experience word, which reached English through Latin medicine, to a Latin clearness word.
intro.cn: 这个词组把希腊语的经验词（经拉丁语医学进入英语）与拉丁语的「清楚」词接起来。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies empiricus and evidentia; Greek peira stands behind the first, and its deeper root is uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了「经验论的」与「清楚」；前者背后是希腊语「尝试」，其更深词根不确定。

items.example: It turns a trial into experience held inside a person.
items.exampleCN: 它把「尝试」变成留在人之内的经验。

items.example: The root behind experience.
items.exampleCN: 这是「经验」背后的词根。

items.example: It passed through Latin into learned English.
items.exampleCN: 它经拉丁语进入学术英语。

items.example: It gave English empiric and empirical.
items.exampleCN: 它给英语提供了「经验论的」与「实证的」。

items.example: It marks empirical as an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 它把「实证」标为形容词。

items.example: The root of evidence.
items.exampleCN: 这是「证据」的词根。

items.example: It became the word for evidence.
items.exampleCN: 它成为「证据」一词。

items.example: It marks the noun evidence.
items.exampleCN: 它标出名词「证据」。

加副词尾，义为「以实证方式」
加主义名词尾，义为「经验主义」
加从事者名词尾，义为「经验论者」
拉丁语「清楚」经法语而来，义为「证据」

definition_zh: 大量有力证据；分量充足的证据；（法律）足以支持行政决定的证据标准
definition_en: a large amount of solid evidence, or the legal standard of evidence sufficient to support an official decision
core_image: 一杆秤上，砝码一块块压下去，横梁终于明显偏向有证据的一侧
scene: 复核委员会翻了三个月材料，认为现有记录已足够厚实，可以支持原来的处理决定。There is substantial evidence that the programme reduced dropout rates.
sceneCN: 这里指分量充足的证据（第 1 个义项：数量与质量都足够的证据）；句意为有大量有力证据表明该项目降低了辍学率。

pos.zh: 大量有力证据；分量充足的证据（不可数）

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语「在下面站立」而来的名词，义为「物质；实质」
由名词加形容词尾构成，义为「大量的；实质的」
加副词尾，义为「大体上；实质上」
加动词尾，义为「证实；使有实据」
再加行为名词尾，义为「证实」
加否定前缀，义为「不牢靠的；微薄的」

senses.title: A large and solid body of evidence
senses.titleCN: 数量与质量都足够的一批证据
senses.definition: a quantity of evidence great enough, and sound enough, to make a conclusion safe
senses.definitionCN: 数量足够、质量可靠，足以使结论站得住的证据
senses.example: There is substantial evidence linking the two trends.
senses.exampleCN: 有大量有力证据把这两种趋势联系起来。
senses.why: Substantial starts from substance, so evidence of this kind has body and weight rather than mere mention.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从「实质」出发，因此这类证据有体量、有重量，而不只是被提了一嘴。

senses.title: A legal standard of sufficiency
senses.definition: the amount of evidence that a court requires to uphold an administrative finding
senses.definitionCN: 法院用来维持行政决定所需的证据数量
senses.example: The appeal failed because the agency's finding met the substantial evidence standard.
senses.exampleCN: 上诉失败，因为该机构的认定达到了实质证据标准。
senses.why: Administrative law needs a threshold, and this phrase is the name of that threshold in many systems.
senses.whyCN: 行政法需要一个门槛，这个词组就是许多法域里那道门槛的名字。

senses.title: Evidence of real moment
senses.definition: evidence that matters to the outcome rather than being peripheral
senses.definitionCN: 对结果有影响、而非边缘性的证据
senses.example: The court ignored the noise because it was not substantial evidence.
senses.exampleCN: 法院忽略了那些杂音，因为它们不是有分量的证据。
senses.why: Substance means what stands under a thing, and evidence with substance is what the decision actually rests on.
senses.whyCN: 「实质」指托在事物下面的东西，有实质的证据才是决定真正依托的东西。

senses.title: Enough to justify action
senses.definition: evidence strong enough for an authority to act without waiting for certainty
senses.definitionCN: 强到足以让主管机关不必等待确定性即可行动的证据
senses.example: Inspectors found substantial evidence of unsafe wiring.
senses.exampleCN: 检查人员发现了大量不安全布线的证据。
senses.why: Action cannot wait for proof beyond doubt, so the phrase marks the point where evidence is enough to move.
senses.whyCN: 行动等不到毫无疑义的证明，这个词组标出的正是「证据够用、可以动手」的那一点。

senses.title: A substantial body of research
senses.definition: an accumulated set of studies that together form a weighty record
senses.definitionCN: 累积起来形成有分量记录的一批研究
senses.example: Substantial evidence from many studies now supports the treatment.
senses.exampleCN: 目前已有大量研究证据支持这种疗法。
senses.why: One study is a point; many studies form a mass, and the word tracks that accumulation.
senses.whyCN: 一项研究是一个点，许多研究聚成一块体量，这个词正描述这种积累。

senses.title: Convincing evidence in evaluation
senses.titleCN: 评估中令人信服的证据
senses.definition: evidence that persuades an evaluator that a programme worked
senses.definitionCN: 使评估者相信某项目确实有效的证据
senses.example: The evaluation reported substantial evidence of improved attendance.
senses.exampleCN: 评估报告称有大量证据表明出勤率提高。
senses.why: Evaluation asks whether a change can be credited to the programme, and substantial evidence answers yes with weight.
senses.whyCN: 评估要问变化能否归功于项目，大量有力证据就是以分量回答「能」。

senses.title: Evidence that is not trivial
senses.definition: evidence above the level of anecdote or isolated illustration
senses.definitionCN: 高于轶事或孤立举例水平的证据
senses.example: A few complaints are not substantial evidence of a systemic fault.
senses.exampleCN: 几起投诉不足以构成系统性缺陷的大量证据。
senses.why: The word draws a line under trivia, since what has no substance cannot carry a conclusion.
senses.whyCN: 这个词在琐碎之下划了一道线：没有实质的东西撑不起结论。

senses.title: Evidence supporting a judgment on the merits
senses.definition: evidence that a reviewing court accepts as adequate to sustain the decision under review
senses.definitionCN: 复审法院认为足以维持被审查决定的证据
senses.example: Judges asked whether the record contained substantial evidence.
senses.exampleCN: 法官们询问案卷中是否有实质证据。
senses.why: Review is limited, and the phrase tells the court how much deference to give the first decision-maker.
senses.whyCN: 复审有限度，这个词组告诉法院应给初审决定者多少尊重。

intro.en: Substantial evidence joins a Latin word for what stands underneath a thing to a Latin word for clearness. Evidence with substance is evidence heavy enough to stand under a decision.
intro.cn: 这个词组把拉丁语中表示「站在事物下面之物」的词，与表示「清楚」的词接在一起：有实质的证据，就是重到能托住一项决定的证据。

items.en: Stare meant to stand, and it stands behind stable, statue and substance.
items.cn: 这个词根意为「站立」，英语中「稳定」「雕像」「实质」等词都出自它。

items.en: With the prefix meaning under, the noun named what stands beneath appearances, hence real being and matter.
items.cn: 加上表示「在下」的前缀，这个名词指站在表象之下的东西，因而指真实存在与物质。

items.en: The adjective meant having substance, and English substantial kept both the sense of solid and the sense of considerable.
items.cn: 这个形容词意为「有实质的」，英语保留了「结实」与「可观」两层意思。

items.en: Substance entered through French for matter, essence and property, giving the adjective a wide base.
items.cn: 这个词经法语进入英语，指物质、本质与财产，为该形容词提供了宽泛的基础。

items.en: Evidentia meant clearness, and evidence became the material that makes a fact clear.
items.cn: 这个词意为「清楚」，「证据」遂指使事实清楚的材料。

items.en: American review statutes fixed substantial evidence as the test for upholding agency findings; the phrase's earlier history is uncertain.
items.cn: 美国复审立法把「实质证据」固定为维持机关认定的标准；该短语更早的历史不确定。

note.en: The first group belongs to the substance family; the second group names evidence of other strengths and sources.
note.cn: 第一组属于「实质」同族；第二组指其他强度与来源的证据。

entries.definition: Matter, or the essential point of a thing.
entries.definitionCN: 指物质，或事物的要点。

entries.definition: Large in amount, or solid in make.
entries.definitionCN: 指数量大或质地坚实的。

entries.definition: To a large degree, or in essential respects.
entries.definitionCN: 指在很大程度上，或就实质而言。

entries.definition: To prove or give evidence for a claim.
entries.definitionCN: 指为某一主张提供证明。

entries.definition: Concerning the essential content rather than procedure.
entries.definitionCN: 指关涉实质内容而非程序的。

entries.definition: Thin, weak or lacking solidity.
entries.definitionCN: 指单薄、虚弱或缺乏坚实性的。

entries.definition: Enough evidence to meet a stated threshold, without the sense of weight.
entries.definitionCN: 指足以达到某门槛的证据，不含分量之意。

entries.definition: Evidence that persuades a reader or jury, measured by effect.
entries.definitionCN: 指能说服读者或陪审团的证据，按效果衡量。

entries.definition: Evidence so strong that it forces a conclusion.
entries.definitionCN: 指强到逼出结论的证据。

entries.definition: Evidence from observation, defined by source rather than weight.
entries.definitionCN: 指来自观察的证据，按来源而非分量界定。

entries.definition: Independent support that confirms an existing account.
entries.definitionCN: 指确认既有说法的独立支持。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the scale loaded with weights, the legal threshold and the distinction from the other evidence phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用压满砝码的秤、法律门槛，以及与其他证据词组的区别。

normal.en: Substance is what stands under a thing, so substantial evidence is what a decision can stand on.
normal.cn: 实质是托在事物下面的东西，所以大量有力证据是决定可以站上去的东西。

normal.en: The legal phrase is «the substantial evidence standard», a fixed test in administrative review.
normal.cn: 法律上的固定说法是「实质证据标准」，是行政复审中的固定检验。

normal.en: Substantial evidence is about weight and amount; empirical evidence is about where it came from.
normal.cn: 大量有力证据说的是分量与数量，实证证据说的是来源。

normal.en: A substantial body of evidence means many studies pointing the same way.
normal.cn: 「大量累积的证据」指许多研究指向同一方向。

normal.en: Substantial also means large, so the phrase can simply mean «a lot of solid evidence».
normal.cn: 这个词也有「大量」之义，所以这个词组也可直译为「很多扎实的证据」。

abstract.en: A scale does not argue; it simply tilts, and the tilt is the judgment.
abstract.cn: 秤不会争辩，它只是倾斜，而倾斜就是判断。

abstract.en: Enough weight can settle a question without answering it perfectly, which is the whole logic of a threshold.
abstract.cn: 足够的重量能了结问题，却不必完美回答它，这正是门槛的全部逻辑。

abstract.en: Evidence with no substance is weather in a courtroom: everyone feels it and nobody can build on it.
abstract.cn: 没有实质的证据就像法庭里的天气：人人感觉得到，却没人能拿它盖东西。

examples.en: There is substantial evidence that the drug lowers blood pressure.
examples.cn: 有大量有力证据表明这种药能降低血压。

examples.en: The tribunal found substantial evidence of unfair dismissal.
examples.cn: 该裁判庭认定存在不公平解雇的实质证据。

examples.en: Substantial evidence now challenges the old model.
examples.cn: 如今有大量有力证据在挑战旧模型。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「实质」是站在下面的东西，「证据」是看清的材料：材料厚到能托住决定，就是大量有力证据

root: 「实质」来自拉丁语 substantia「站在下面之物」，由 sub-「在下」与 stare「站立」构成；「证据」来自拉丁语 evidentia「清楚」。美国行政复审立法把「实质证据」固定为维持机关认定的标准；更早历史不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses run from weight to review: a large solid body, the legal sufficiency test, evidence of real moment, enough to justify action, accumulated research, convincing evaluation data, non-trivial evidence, and support for a judgment on the merits.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从分量延伸到复审：大量扎实证据、法律充分性标准、真正有分量的证据、足以支持行动、累积研究、可信评估数据、非琐碎证据、支持实体裁判的证据。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: weights are stacked on one pan until the beam visibly tilts toward the side with evidence.
core.cn: 核心意象：砝码一块块压上秤盘，横梁终于明显偏向有证据的一侧。

branches.en: THE WEIGHT: evidence with body behind it, resting under the conclusion.
branches.cn: 分量：背后有实体的证据，托在结论下面。

branches.en: THE LEGAL THRESHOLD: the amount a court needs to uphold a finding or decision.
branches.cn: 法律门槛：法院维持认定或决定所需的证据量。

branches.en: THE PERMISSION TO ACT: evidence strong enough for an authority or evaluator to move.
branches.cn: 行动的许可：强到足以让主管机关或评估者动手的证据。

branches.en: THE ACCUMULATED MASS: many studies forming one heavy record.
branches.cn: 积累的体量：许多研究汇成一份沉重的记录。

branches.en: THE LINE ABOVE TRIVIA: evidence that is more than anecdote or isolated example.
branches.cn: 琐碎之上的线：不只是轶事或孤立例子的证据。

intro.en: The phrase joins a Latin word for standing underneath to a Latin word for clearness, so its two halves still mean weight and visibility.
intro.cn: 这个词组把拉丁语中「站在下面」的词与「清楚」的词接起来，两半至今都表示重量与可见性。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies substantia and evidentia; the legal sense of the phrase is modern and largely statutory.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了「实质」与「清楚」；该短语的法律义属现代用法，主要来自成文法。

items.example: It turns standing into standing underneath.
items.exampleCN: 它把「站立」变成「站在下面」。

items.example: The root of substance and stable.
items.exampleCN: 这是「实质」与「稳定」的词根。

items.example: It became English substance.
items.exampleCN: 它成为英语的「实质」。

items.example: It gave English substantial.
items.exampleCN: 它给英语提供了「大量的；实质的」。

items.example: It marks substantial as an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 它把「实质」标为形容词。

items.example: It forms substantiate, to give substance to a claim.
items.exampleCN: 它构成「证实」，即为主张提供实质。

items.example: It became the word for evidence.
items.exampleCN: 它成为「证据」一词。

items.example: It marks the noun evidence.
items.exampleCN: 它标出名词「证据」。

derivatives.zh: 拉丁「站在下面之物」经法语而来，义为「物质；实质」
加形容词尾，义为「大量的；实质的」
加副词尾，义为「大体上」
加动词尾，义为「证实」
加行为名词尾，义为「证实」
加否定前缀，义为「单薄的」

definition_zh: 理由说明；根本缘由；对某项决策、方法或设计背后道理的系统解释
definition_en: the set of reasons that explains why a decision, method or design was chosen
core_image: 一份文件末尾附着一页说明，把每个选择背后的那条道理逐条写清，签字栏留在下方
scene: 评审会上，设计者没有只讲做了什么，而是把每一步选择背后的道理写在附页上。The report explains the rationale behind the new testing rule.
sceneCN: 这里指决策背后的道理说明（第 1 个义项：对选择理由的系统说明）；句意为报告解释了新测试规则背后的理由。

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语「计算、理性」而来的形容词，义为「理性的」
加副词尾，义为「理性地」
加表示性质的名词尾，义为「理性」
加动词尾，义为「使合理化；为……找理由」
再加行为名词尾，义为「合理化；辩解」
加否定前缀，义为「不理性的」

senses.title: The reasons behind a decision
senses.definition: the thinking that explains why a particular choice was made
senses.definitionCN: 说明为何作出某一选择的思考
senses.example: The memo sets out the rationale for closing the branch.
senses.exampleCN: 备忘录陈述了关闭该分行的理由。
senses.why: Ratio is reckoning, and a rationale is the reckoning written out after the choice has been made.
senses.whyCN: 这个词根意为「计算」，理由说明就是选择作出后写出来的那笔账。

senses.title: A formal statement of justification
senses.definition: an official written account that defends a decision to those who must approve it
senses.definitionCN: 向需要批准者辩护某项决定的正式书面说明
senses.example: Applicants must attach a rationale for the funding request.
senses.exampleCN: 申请人必须附上拨款请求的理由说明。
senses.why: Institutions require reasons on the record, and that record is the formal form of this word.
senses.whyCN: 机构要求在案卷中留下理由，而这份案卷就是这个词的正式形态。

senses.title: The reasoning section of a report
senses.definition: the part of a report or proposal that explains why the approach was adopted
senses.definitionCN: 报告或提案中解释为何采用该做法的那一部分
senses.example: Section two of the report is devoted to the rationale.
senses.exampleCN: 报告第二节专门说明理由。
senses.why: A document has a place for its reasoning, and the word names that section rather than its content alone.
senses.whyCN: 文件为推理留有一个位置，这个词也指那一节，而不只是内容。

senses.title: Design rationale in engineering
senses.definition: the recorded reasons for each technical choice in a design
senses.definitionCN: 对设计中每项技术选择的记录理由
senses.example: The design rationale explains why the lighter alloy was rejected.
senses.exampleCN: 设计理由说明了为何没有采用更轻的合金。
senses.why: Engineering keeps a trace of decisions so that later changes do not undo what was carefully chosen.
senses.whyCN: 工程保留决策痕迹，以免后来的改动推翻当初的精心选择。

senses.title: The principle behind a policy
senses.definition: the stated principle that justifies a rule and guides its application
senses.definitionCN: 为某项规则提供依据并指导其适用的明示原则
senses.example: The rationale of the tax is to discourage speculation.
senses.exampleCN: 这项税收的理据是抑制投机。
senses.why: A rule without a principle is arbitrary, so policy writing always asks for the rationale.
senses.whyCN: 没有原则的规则是任意的，所以政策写作总要问其理据。

senses.title: The purpose of a method
senses.definition: the explanation of what a procedure is meant to achieve and why that matters
senses.definitionCN: 说明某程序要达到什么、为何重要的解释
senses.example: The methods chapter gives the rationale for using interviews.
senses.exampleCN: 方法一章给出了采用访谈的理由。
senses.why: A method can be copied without understanding, and stating its rationale prevents blind copying.
senses.whyCN: 方法可以被不懂的人照搬，说明理据正是为了防止盲搬。

senses.title: A principle offered in ethics
senses.definition: the moral principle that is said to justify an action or a rule
senses.definitionCN: 被用来为某一行为或规则辩护的道德原则
senses.example: The committee questioned the ethical rationale for the trial.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会质疑该试验的伦理理据。
senses.why: Ethics asks for the principle, not merely the preference, which is the sharpest use of the word.
senses.whyCN: 伦理学要的是原则而非偏好，这是这个词最锋利的用法。

senses.title: The articulated reason, not the cause
senses.titleCN: 说出的理由，而非单纯的原因
senses.definition: a reason that has been consciously formed and stated, as distinct from a mere cause or trigger
senses.definitionCN: 经有意识整理并说出的理由，区别于单纯的原因或触发因素
senses.example: Fatigue was the cause, but the stated rationale was a scheduling conflict.
senses.exampleCN: 疲劳是原因，但说出的理由是日程冲突。
senses.why: This sense marks the word's boundary: a cause can be unknown to the actor, while a rationale is always someone's account.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项标出词的边界：原因可能连当事人也不知道，而理由总是某人的说法。

intro.en: Rationale is the noun form of rational, from Latin ratio, reckoning or reason. English took the neuter form of the Latin adjective and used it for the explanatory statement of reasons behind a choice.
intro.cn: 这个词是「理性的」的名词形态，来自拉丁语 ratio「计算、理性」。英语取该拉丁形容词的中性形式，用来指一项选择背后说明理由的文字。

items.en: Reri meant to reckon or think, and it stands behind ratio and the whole family of rational words.
items.cn: 这个词意为「计算、思考」，是 ratio 与整个「理性」词族的来源。

items.en: Ratio named reckoning, account and reason, and it also meant the relation between things.
items.cn: 这个词指计算、账目与理性，也指事物之间的关系。

items.en: The adjective meant belonging to reason, and its neuter form named a reasoned account.
items.cn: 这个形容词意为「属于理性的」，其中性形式指有理由的说明。

items.en: English used rationale for an explanatory principle, especially in theology and law; the first record is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语用这个词指解释性原则，尤见于神学与法律；最早记录不确定。

items.en: The adjective rational describes a person or act; the noun rationale names the account of reasons itself.
items.cn: 形容词描述人或行为，名词则指理由说明本身。

items.en: Design, policy and research writing made the word a standard heading for the justification of a choice.
items.cn: 设计、政策与研究写作把这个词变成论证某项选择的标准标题。

note.en: The first group belongs to the reason family or looks close; the second group names grounds and explanations of different kinds.
note.cn: 第一组属于「理性」同族或形近；第二组指不同类型的根据与解释。

entries.definition: Able to reason, or based on reason rather than feeling.
entries.definitionCN: 指能推理的，或以理性而非情感为依据的。

entries.definition: In a reasoned way.
entries.definitionCN: 指以有理有据的方式。

entries.definition: The quality of being reasoned or logical.
entries.definitionCN: 指有理据、合逻辑的性质。

entries.definition: To make something seem reasonable, often after the fact.
entries.definitionCN: 指使某事显得合理，常是事后为之。

entries.definition: A plausible but self-serving explanation.
entries.definitionCN: 指看似合理实则自利的解释。

entries.definition: A numerical relation between two quantities.
entries.definitionCN: 指两个数量之间的数值关系。

entries.definition: Any cause or motive, whether stated or not; broader and less formal.
entries.definitionCN: 指任何原因或动机，无论是否说出；更宽、更不正式。

entries.definition: A defence showing that an action was right, stronger in moral weight.
entries.definitionCN: 指证明行为正当的辩护，道德分量更重。

entries.definition: The stated basis for a belief or legal action.
entries.definitionCN: 指信念或法律行动的明示依据。

entries.definition: The foundation on which a claim or decision rests.
entries.definitionCN: 指主张或决定所依托的基础。

entries.definition: A statement that makes something understandable, not necessarily a justification.
entries.definitionCN: 指使某事物可理解的陈述，未必是辩护。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the appended page of reasons, the design record and the distinction from a plain cause.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用附在文件后的理由页、设计记录，以及与单纯原因的区分。

normal.en: Rationale is the noun of rational, so it names the written reckoning behind a choice.
normal.cn: 它是「理性的」的名词，因此指一项选择背后写出来的那笔账。

normal.en: The fixed academic phrases are «the rationale for» and «the rationale behind».
normal.cn: 学术中的固定说法是「……的理由」与「背后的道理」。

normal.en: Design rationale is a real engineering practice, kept so later changes do not undo earlier reasoning.
normal.cn: 「设计理由」是真实的工程实践，留存它是为防止后来的改动推翻早先的推理。

normal.en: A rationale can be bad, but it must be stated; a cause need not be known at all.
normal.cn: 理由可能很糟，但必须被说出；原因则可以完全不被知道。

normal.en: The plural rationales appears in review forms, where each choice needs its own paragraph.
normal.cn: 复数形式出现在评审表里，每个选择都要有自己的一段。

abstract.en: A rationale is the skeleton of a decision left visible on purpose.
abstract.cn: 理由说明是刻意留在外面的决策骨架。

abstract.en: Institutions run on stated reasons, because a reason can be argued with while a preference cannot.
abstract.cn: 机构靠说出的理由运转，因为理由可以被争辩，偏好不能。

abstract.en: The gap between the real cause and the stated rationale is where most self-deception lives.
abstract.cn: 真实原因与说出的理由之间的缝隙，正是大多数自欺栖身之处。

examples.en: The proposal gives a clear rationale for expanding the programme.
examples.cn: 提案为扩大该项目给出了清楚的理由说明。

examples.en: Reviewers asked for the rationale behind the choice of method.
examples.cn: 审稿人要求说明选择该方法背后的道理。

examples.en: The design rationale records why the cheaper material was rejected.
examples.cn: 设计理由记录了为何没有采用更便宜的材料。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「瑞羞奈尔」——把「理」由一条条写「奈」在纸上，供人核对，就是理由说明

root: 拉丁语 ratio「计算、理性」出自动词 reri「计算、思考」，其形容词 rationalis 的中性形式在十六世纪进入英语，指解释性原则；现代设计、政策与研究写作用它作为论证选择的标准标题。最早记录年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses run from the private reason to the public account: the reasons behind a decision, a formal justification, a report section, a design record, a policy principle, a method's purpose, an ethical ground, and the stated reason as distinct from a cause.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从私下理由走向公开说明：决策背后的理由、正式辩护、报告章节、设计记录、政策原则、方法用意、伦理依据，以及区别于单纯原因的「说出的理由」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a page of numbered reasons is clipped behind a decision, each line answering a question someone will ask.
core.cn: 核心意象：一页编号的理由附在决定后面，每一行都在回答别人会问的问题。

branches.en: THE REASONING ITSELF: the thinking behind a choice, and its difference from a bare cause.
branches.cn: 推理本身：选择背后的思考，以及它与单纯原因的区别。

branches.en: THE WRITTEN ACCOUNT: the formal justification and the section that carries it.
branches.cn: 书面说明：正式的辩护与承载它的章节。

branches.en: THE METHOD'S WHY: a design record and the stated purpose of a procedure.
branches.cn: 方法之因：设计记录与程序的明示用意。

branches.en: THE POLICY PRINCIPLE: the rule's justifying principle.
branches.cn: 政策原则：为规则提供依据的原则。

branches.en: THE ETHICAL GROUND: the moral principle offered in defence of an act.
branches.cn: 伦理依据：为行为辩护而提出的道德原则。

intro.en: Rationale is a Latin reason word in noun form, and its family covers reckoning, ratio and rationality.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语「理性」名词形态，其词族覆盖计算、比率与理性。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies reri, ratio and rationalis; the English noun is the neuter adjective used as a name for a reasoned account.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了「计算」「理性」与「理性的」；英语名词是中性形容词用作「有理据说明」的名称。

items.example: The deepest root of the family.
items.exampleCN: 这是该词族最深的词根。

items.example: It became English ratio and reason.
items.exampleCN: 它成为英语的「比率」与「理由」。

items.example: Its neuter gave the English noun.
items.exampleCN: 其中性形式给出这个英语名词。

items.example: It marks rational as an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 它把「理性」标为形容词。

items.example: It forms rationality.
items.exampleCN: 它构成「理性」这一名词。

items.example: It forms rationalize.
items.exampleCN: 它构成「使合理化」。

items.example: It forms irrational, the opposite.
items.exampleCN: 它构成反义词「不理性的」。

items.example: It forms rationally and rationally.
items.exampleCN: 它构成副词形式。

derivatives.zh: 加形容词尾，义为「理性的」
加副词尾，义为「理性地」
加性质名词尾，义为「理性」
加动词尾，义为「使合理化」
加行为名词尾，义为「合理化」
加否定前缀，义为「不理性的」

definition_zh: 因果关系；一个事件或变量引起另一个事件或变量的联系
definition_en: a link in which one event or variable brings about another
core_image: 一排多米诺骨牌，第一块倒下时推倒第二块，倒下的方向清楚可见
scene: 研究者发现，气温升高之后冰淇淋销量随之上升，但不敢直接说二者有因果联系。The study tested whether a causal relationship exists between the two variables.
sceneCN: 这里指一个变量引起另一个变量的联系（第 1 个义项：引起与被引起的联系）；句意为这项研究检验两个变量之间是否存在因果关系。

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语「原因、案件」而来的动词，义为「引起；导致」
加形容词尾，义为「因果的」
加副词尾，义为「在因果上」
加行为名词尾，义为「因果作用；引起」
加形容词尾，义为「使然的；致因的」
由拉丁语「带回」而来的名词，义为「关系」
由「关系」加表示状态的名词尾构成，义为「联系；关系」

senses.title: One event bringing about another
senses.titleCN: 一个事件引起另一个事件
senses.definition: a link in which the occurrence of one event makes the other happen
senses.definitionCN: 一个事件的发生使另一事件得以发生的联系
senses.example: The court accepted a causal relationship between the leak and the illness.
senses.exampleCN: 法院认可了泄漏与疾病之间的因果关系。
senses.why: Cause is the active side and relationship is the link, so the phrase joins the pushing to the connecting.
senses.whyCN: 「原因」是主动的一面，「关系」是那条连接，这个词组把推与连接在一起。

senses.title: A directional link between variables
senses.titleCN: 变量之间的方向性联系
senses.definition: a connection in which a change in one variable produces a change in another
senses.definitionCN: 一个变量的变化引起另一变量变化的联系
senses.example: The model assumes a causal relationship running from income to health.
senses.exampleCN: 该模型假定存在从收入指向健康的因果关系。
senses.why: Direction is what separates causation from mere association, and the phrase always implies an arrow.
senses.whyCN: 方向正是因果与单纯关联的分界，这个词组总暗含一支箭头。

senses.title: A causal chain
senses.definition: a sequence in which each step brings about the next, so that the first reaches the last through intermediates
senses.definitionCN: 每一步引起下一步、最初一环经中间环节到达最后一环的序列
senses.example: A causal relationship between rainfall and crop failure runs through soil moisture.
senses.exampleCN: 降雨与歉收之间的因果关系经由土壤湿度这一环。
senses.why: Long causes act through middle steps, and the phrase can name the whole chain rather than a single jump.
senses.whyCN: 远因通过中间环节起作用，这个词组可以指整条链，而不只是单次跳跃。

senses.title: A claim tested by experiment
senses.titleCN: 由实验检验的因果主张
senses.definition: a statement that one condition causes another, which an intervention is designed to test
senses.definitionCN: 某条件引起另一条件的主张，并用干预来检验它
senses.example: Random assignment lets the trial test a causal relationship rather than describe one.
senses.exampleCN: 随机分配让试验得以检验因果关系，而不只是描述它。
senses.why: Only an intervention can show that changing the cause changes the effect, which is why experiments exist.
senses.whyCN: 只有干预才能显示改变原因会改变结果，这正是实验存在的理由。

senses.title: A legal causal link
senses.definition: the connection the law requires between an act and a harm before liability attaches
senses.definitionCN: 法律要求在行为与损害之间具备、责任才成立的联系
senses.example: The plaintiff had to prove a causal relationship between the defect and the injury.
senses.exampleCN: 原告必须证明缺陷与伤害之间的因果关系。
senses.why: Law asks whether the harm would have happened but for the act, a narrower test than scientific causation.
senses.whyCN: 法律问的是若没有该行为损害是否仍会发生，这比科学上的因果更窄。

senses.title: A risk factor linked to disease
senses.titleCN: 与疾病相连的风险因素
senses.definition: an association in medicine between an exposure and the later onset of a condition
senses.definitionCN: 医学中暴露因素与后来发病之间的关联
senses.example: Epidemiologists found a causal relationship between smoking and lung cancer.
senses.exampleCN: 流行病学家发现了吸烟与肺癌之间的因果关系。
senses.why: Medicine must act before mechanisms are fully known, so it often states the relationship before the process.
senses.whyCN: 医学必须在机制完全清楚之前行动，因此常先陈述关系，再谈过程。

senses.title: A link inferred from correlation
senses.definition: a causal reading that researchers draw from a strong association, subject to further checks
senses.definitionCN: 研究者从强关联中得出的因果解读，仍待进一步检验
senses.example: A causal relationship was inferred, but only after confounders were controlled.
senses.exampleCN: 因果关系是被推断出来的，而且是在控制混淆因素之后。
senses.why: Correlation suggests, and causal language converts the suggestion into a claim that must then be defended.
senses.whyCN: 相关只提示，因果措辞把提示变成需要辩护的主张。

senses.title: A two-way causal relationship
senses.definition: a link in which each side influences the other over time
senses.definitionCN: 双方随时间相互影响的联系
senses.example: Income and health show a causal relationship in both directions.
senses.exampleCN: 收入与健康呈现出双向的因果关系。
senses.why: Feedback loops are common in social systems, so the arrow sometimes has to be drawn twice.
senses.whyCN: 社会系统中反馈环很常见，所以箭头有时得画两次。

intro.en: Causal relationship joins the Latin word for cause to a Latin word for carrying back. The first half supplies the push, the second the link that carries the push to its result.
intro.cn: 这个词组把拉丁语中表示「原因」的词，与表示「带回」的词接在一起：前一半提供推力，后一半提供把推力带到结果的连接。

items.en: Causa meant cause, reason and also a legal case, since a case is a matter brought before a court.
items.cn: 这个词指原因、理由，也指案件，因为案件是被带到法庭前的事。

items.en: Late Latin formed the adjective for what belongs to a cause, and English causal came from it.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语为「属于原因的」造出形容词，英语的「因果的」由此而来。

items.en: Cause entered through French for both the reason of an event and the matter of a lawsuit.
items.cn: 这个词经法语进入英语，既指事件的原因，也指诉讼案件。

items.en: Ferre meant to carry, and with the prefix meaning back it produced referre, to bring back or relate.
items.cn: 这个词根意为「搬运」，加上表示「回」的前缀后构成「带回、关联」。

items.en: Relatio named a carrying back, hence a report or a connection between things.
items.cn: 这个词指「带回」，因而指报告或事物之间的联系。

items.en: Relation entered in the fourteenth century and relationship followed later; the exact first date of the compound is uncertain.
items.cn: 「关系」在十四世纪进入英语，「联系」随后出现；该复合词确切的最早年代不确定。

note.en: The first group belongs to the cause family or looks close; the second group names associations and links of different force.
note.cn: 第一组属于「原因」同族或形近；第二组指力度不同的关联与连接。

entries.definition: The event or condition that produces an effect.
entries.definitionCN: 指产生结果的事件或条件。

entries.definition: Relating to cause and effect.
entries.definitionCN: 指与因果有关的。

entries.definition: In terms of cause and effect.
entries.definitionCN: 指就因果关系而言。

entries.definition: The act or process of causing.
entries.definitionCN: 指引起的行为或过程。

entries.definition: Producing an effect, often used in grammar.
entries.definitionCN: 指致因的，常用于语法。

entries.definition: Relaxed or accidental; its root is falling, not causing.
entries.definitionCN: 指随意或偶然的；词根是「落下」，与致因无关。

entries.definition: A statistical association without a claim about direction or cause.
entries.definitionCN: 指统计上的关联，不主张方向或原因。

entries.definition: Any observed connection, weaker than a causal claim.
entries.definitionCN: 指任何观察到的连接，比因果主张弱。

entries.definition: The process through which the cause acts, which explains the relationship.
entries.definitionCN: 指原因起作用的过程，它解释这种关系。

entries.definition: The outcome produced by a cause.
entries.definitionCN: 指原因产生的结果。

entries.definition: A relation in which one thing relies on another, not necessarily causal.
entries.definitionCN: 指一物依赖另一物的关系，未必是因果。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the falling dominoes, the arrow of direction and the legal but-for test.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用倒下的多米诺、方向箭头与法律上的「若没有」检验。

normal.en: Causal means belonging to a cause, so a causal relationship is the link a cause travels along.
normal.cn: 「因果的」意为属于原因的，所以因果关系就是原因走过的连接。

normal.en: The fixed phrase is «a causal relationship between» two variables.
normal.cn: 固定说法是「两个变量之间的因果关系」。

normal.en: Dominoes are the clearest picture: each fall is both an effect and the next cause.
normal.cn: 多米诺是最清楚的画面：每一次倒下既是结果，也是下一次的原因。

normal.en: Law tests it with «but for»: would the harm have happened without the act?
normal.cn: 法律用「若没有」检验：没有该行为，损害还会发生吗？

normal.en: Correlation is an observation; causal relationship is a claim about direction.
normal.cn: 相关是观察，因果关系是关于方向的主张。

abstract.en: A causal relationship is a river with a direction; correlation is only a map of wet ground.
abstract.cn: 因果关系是有方向的河流，相关只是湿地的一张图。

abstract.en: Cause and effect can trade places over time, and then the phrase must be drawn with two arrows.
abstract.cn: 原因与结果会随时间互换位置，此时这个词组得画上两支箭头。

abstract.en: Naming a relationship causal is a promise to explain how the push travels.
abstract.cn: 把一种关系称为因果，就是承诺要解释这股推力如何传递。

examples.en: The data show a strong correlation but do not prove a causal relationship.
examples.cn: 数据显示出强相关，却未证明因果关系。

examples.en: Randomised trials are designed to establish a causal relationship.
examples.cn: 随机试验旨在确立因果关系。

examples.en: Researchers found a causal relationship between sleep and test scores.
examples.cn: 研究者发现睡眠与考试成绩之间存在因果关系。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「原因」是推手，「关系」是连线：推手通过连线把力量送到结果，就是因果关系

root: 「原因」来自拉丁语 causa「原因；案件」；「关系」来自拉丁语 relatio「带回」，其动词 ferre 意为「搬运」。「因果的」为晚期拉丁语形容词，英语十三世纪起用「原因」，十四世纪起用「关系」；复合词确切最早年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses run from a single push to a two-way loop: one event causing another, a directional variable link, a causal chain, an experimental claim, a legal link, a medical risk link, a link inferred from correlation, and a reciprocal relationship.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从单次推动延伸到双向回路：一事件引起另一事件、变量间的方向联系、因果链、实验主张、法律联系、医学风险联系、由相关推断的联系、双向关系。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a row of dominoes falls in one direction, each block both struck and striking.
core.cn: 核心意象：一排多米诺朝同一方向倒下，每一块既被撞倒也撞倒下一块。

branches.en: THE PUSH AND THE ARROW: one event making another happen, with a clear direction.
branches.cn: 推力与箭头：一个事件使另一事件发生，方向清楚。

branches.en: THE LONG CHAIN: the cause reaching its effect through intermediate steps.
branches.cn: 长链：原因经中间环节抵达结果。

branches.en: THE TESTED AND INFERRED CLAIM: a relationship tried by intervention or read from association.
branches.cn: 被检验与推断的主张：经干预检验或从关联读出的关系。

branches.en: THE APPLIED LINK: legal liability and medical risk.
branches.cn: 应用中的联系：法律责任与医学风险。

branches.en: THE TWO-WAY LOOP: mutual influence drawn with two arrows.
branches.cn: 双向回路：以两支箭头画出的相互影响。

intro.en: The phrase joins a Latin cause word to a Latin carrying word; direction is supplied by cause, connection by relation.
intro.cn: 这个词组把拉丁语的「原因」与「搬运」接起来：方向由原因提供，连接由关系提供。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies causa and relatio; the modern compound is English, and its first record is uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了「原因」与「关系」；现代复合词是英语构词，最早记录不确定。

items.example: The source of cause and causal.
items.exampleCN: 这是「原因」与「因果的」的来源。

items.example: It gave English causal.
items.exampleCN: 它给英语提供了「因果的」。

items.example: The root behind relation.
items.exampleCN: 这是「关系」背后的词根。

items.example: It turns carrying into carrying back.
items.exampleCN: 它把「搬运」变成「带回」。

items.example: It became English relation.
items.exampleCN: 它成为英语的「关系」。

items.example: It forms relationship from relation.
items.exampleCN: 它由「关系」构成「联系」。

items.example: It marks causal as an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 它把「因果」标为形容词。

items.example: It forms causation.
items.exampleCN: 它构成「因果作用」。

加形容词尾，义为「因果的」
加副词尾，义为「在因果上」
加行为名词尾，义为「因果作用」
加形容词尾，义为「致因的」
拉丁「带回」经法语而来的名词，义为「关系」
加状态名词尾，义为「联系」

definition_zh: 因果机制；原因通过一连串中间环节产生结果的运作过程
definition_en: the process through which a cause produces its effect, step by step
core_image: 齿轮箱剖开，第一枚齿轮转动，依次带动第二、第三枚，最后拉动一根连杆
scene: 实验显示两种药物都有效，但研究者还想弄清它究竟通过哪条生理路径起作用。The paper proposes a causal mechanism linking sleep loss to poor decisions.
sceneCN: 这里指原因起作用的中间过程（第 1 个义项：从原因到结果的一连串环节）；句意为论文提出了一条把睡眠不足与糟糕决策联系起来的因果机制。

collocations.zh: 把……联系起来的因果机制

derivatives.zh: 由希腊语「装置、机械」而来的名词，义为「机制；机械装置」
加形容词尾，义为「机械式的；机制层面的」
加动词尾，义为「使机械化」
加行为名词尾，义为「机械化」
同源名词，经拉丁语而来的「机器」

senses.title: The process from cause to effect
senses.definition: the sequence of steps through which an initial condition produces its outcome
senses.definitionCN: 初始条件经由产生结果的一连串步骤
senses.example: The study names a causal mechanism rather than merely reporting a correlation.
senses.exampleCN: 这项研究指出了一种因果机制，而不只是报告相关。
senses.why: A mechanism is a working device, and calling it causal asks how the device runs, not just what it produces.
senses.whyCN: 机制是一台运转的装置，称其为因果，问的是它如何运转，而不只是产出什么。

senses.title: An intervening chain of steps
senses.titleCN: 起中介作用的一串环节
senses.definition: a series of intermediate changes that carry the influence from cause to effect
senses.definitionCN: 把影响从原因带到结果的一系列中间变化
senses.example: A causal mechanism through soil chemistry explains the crop failure.
senses.exampleCN: 一条经由土壤化学的因果机制解释了歉收。
senses.why: The middle steps are where the explanation lives, since a direct jump is usually just a restatement.
senses.whyCN: 解释就住在中间环节，因为直接跳跃通常只是同义反复。

senses.title: A biological mechanism
senses.definition: a physiological or molecular pathway that produces a bodily effect
senses.definitionCN: 产生身体效应的生理或分子通路
senses.example: The drug's causal mechanism involves blocking a receptor.
senses.exampleCN: 这种药的因果机制涉及阻断一个受体。
senses.why: Physiology describes the body as a system of parts, so «mechanism» is at home there.
senses.whyCN: 生理学把身体描述为由部件组成的系统，因此「机制」在这里最自然。

senses.title: A social mechanism
senses.definition: a social process by which a condition produces a collective outcome
senses.definitionCN: 某条件通过社会过程产生集体结果的机制
senses.example: Sociologists proposed a causal mechanism based on peer imitation.
senses.exampleCN: 社会学家提出了一条基于同伴模仿的因果机制。
senses.why: Social science borrowed the machine word for patterns of action that reliably produce an outcome.
senses.whyCN: 社会科学借来这个机械词，指稳定产生某结果的行为模式。

senses.title: A mechanism confirmed experimentally
senses.definition: a pathway that has been shown to operate under controlled manipulation
senses.definitionCN: 在受控操作下被显示确实运作的通路
senses.example: The team confirmed the causal mechanism by blocking the pathway.
senses.exampleCN: 团队通过阻断该通路确认了这一因果机制。
senses.why: Blocking a step and watching the effect vanish is the strongest proof that the step matters.
senses.whyCN: 阻断某一步、看效应消失，是该步骤起作用的最强证明。

senses.title: A hypothesised mechanism
senses.definition: a proposed pathway that is plausible but not yet demonstrated
senses.definitionCN: 看似合理但尚未被证实的通路
senses.example: The paper offers a causal mechanism that no experiment has yet tested.
senses.exampleCN: 论文提出了一条尚无实验检验的因果机制。
senses.why: Explanations often arrive before evidence, and the word can mark a proposal rather than a finding.
senses.whyCN: 解释常先于证据到来，这个词可以标出一个提议，而非一项发现。

senses.title: A mediating pathway in a model
senses.definition: the route through a mediator variable that carries an effect in a statistical model
senses.definitionCN: 统计模型中经由中介变量把效应带过去的路径
senses.example: The causal mechanism runs through a mediating attitude score.
senses.exampleCN: 这条因果机制经由一个中介态度得分。
senses.why: Statistics draws the mechanism as a path, turning the machine picture into arrows between variables.
senses.whyCN: 统计把机制画成路径，把机械画面变成变量之间的箭头。

senses.title: Explanation as against correlation
senses.definition: the account that tells you why an association holds, not only that it holds
senses.definitionCN: 说明关联为何成立、而不只是说明它成立的说法
senses.example: Without a causal mechanism, the finding remains a black box.
senses.exampleCN: 没有因果机制，这一发现仍是一个黑箱。
senses.why: A correlation says two things move together; a mechanism opens the box and shows the gears.
senses.whyCN: 相关说两件事一起动，机制打开箱子，让人看见齿轮。

intro.en: Causal mechanism joins the Latin word for cause to a Greek word for a machine or device. The phrase asks by what working parts a cause delivers its effect.
intro.cn: 这个词组把拉丁语中表示「原因」的词，与希腊语中表示「机械、装置」的词接在一起：它问的是原因通过哪些运转部件把结果送达。

items.en: Mekhane meant a machine, device or contrivance, especially the stage device used to lower a god into a play.
items.cn: 这个词指机械、装置或巧设，尤指戏剧中把神降下的舞台装置。

items.en: The noun for means or expedient stands behind mekhane, but its deeper root is not settled.
items.cn: 表示「手段、办法」的名词是「机械」一词的来源，但其更深词根存疑。

items.en: Latin took the Greek word as machina, and English machine descends from it through French.
items.cn: 拉丁语取来这个词作 machina，英语的「机器」经法语承袭。

items.en: Causa meant cause, reason and legal case, and it supplied the first half of the phrase.
items.cn: 这个词指原因、理由与案件，提供了词组的前一半。

items.en: Mechanism entered English for the parts of a machine and then for any system of working parts.
items.cn: 这个词在十七世纪进入英语，先指机器的部件，后指任何由部件运作的系统。

items.en: The phrase causal mechanism became standard in the twentieth century for the process that links cause and effect; the exact first record is uncertain.
items.cn: 「因果机制」在二十世纪成为标准说法，指连接原因与结果的过程；确切最早记录不确定。

note.en: The first group belongs to the mechanism family; the second group names paths and explanatory concepts.
note.cn: 第一组属于「机制」同族；第二组指路径与解释性概念。

entries.definition: A system of working parts, or the process by which something works.
entries.definitionCN: 指由部件构成的系统，或某物运作的过程。

entries.definition: Explained as a system of mechanical parts.
entries.definitionCN: 指以机械部件系统来解释的。

entries.definition: To replace human work with machinery.
entries.definitionCN: 指用机械取代人力。

entries.definition: The process of replacing labour with machines.
entries.definitionCN: 指以机械取代劳动的过程。

entries.definition: A device with parts that work together.
entries.definitionCN: 指由协同运作的部件组成的装置。

entries.definition: A person who repairs machines.
entries.definitionCN: 指修理机器的人。

entries.definition: The route an influence takes, often drawn as a path model.
entries.definitionCN: 指影响经过的路线，常画成路径模型。

entries.definition: A variable that carries the effect from cause to outcome.
entries.definitionCN: 指把效应从原因带到结果的变量。

entries.definition: A series of changes, without implying that they explain anything.
entries.definitionCN: 指一系列变化，不暗示其具有解释力。

entries.definition: The route by which something passes from one place to another.
entries.definitionCN: 指某物从一处传到另一处的通道。

entries.definition: The link itself, which the mechanism is supposed to explain.
entries.definitionCN: 指联系本身，而机制正是要解释这条联系。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the opened gearbox, the blocked receptor and the path diagram.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用剖开的齿轮箱、被阻断的受体与路径图。

normal.en: Mechanism is a machine word, so a causal mechanism is the machine between cause and effect.
normal.cn: 「机制」是个机械词，所以因果机制就是原因与结果之间的那台机器。

normal.en: The phrase «a causal mechanism linking» is the standard academic form.
normal.cn: 标准学术说法是「把……联系起来的因果机制」。

normal.en: Blocking one step and watching the effect disappear is how mechanisms are confirmed.
normal.cn: 阻断一步、看效应消失，是确认机制的办法。

normal.en: A mechanism answers «how», while a correlation answers only «whether».
normal.cn: 机制回答「如何」，相关只回答「是否」。

normal.en: Mediation analysis draws the mechanism as a path through a middle variable.
normal.cn: 中介分析把机制画成穿过中间变量的路径。

abstract.en: A correlation is a shadow on the wall; a mechanism is the object casting it.
abstract.cn: 相关是墙上的影子，机制是投下影子的物体。

abstract.en: Every black box is a mechanism someone has not opened yet.
abstract.cn: 每个黑箱都是尚无人打开的机制。

abstract.en: The machine picture is honest: effects are produced by parts, not by wishes.
abstract.cn: 机械画面是诚实的：结果由部件产生，不由愿望产生。

examples.en: The researchers identified a causal mechanism involving two enzymes.
examples.cn: 研究者识别出一条涉及两种酶的因果机制。

examples.en: Without a causal mechanism, the association cannot guide policy.
examples.cn: 没有因果机制，这种关联无法指导政策。

examples.en: The model tests a causal mechanism that runs through social trust.
examples.cn: 该模型检验一条经由社会信任的因果机制。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因果」是推力，「机制」是机器：推力在机器里经过一串齿轮，最后落在结果上

root: 「因果」来自拉丁语 causa「原因」；「机制」来自希腊语 mekhane「机械、装置」，表示「手段」的 mekhos 是其来源，但更深来源未定；经拉丁语 machina 与法语进入英语。十七世纪起指机器部件，二十世纪社会科学固定为「连接原因与结果的过程」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses run from the gearbox to the path model: the process from cause to effect, intervening steps, biological and social mechanisms, experimental confirmation, hypothesis, mediation, and explanation as against correlation.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从齿轮箱延伸到路径模型：从原因到结果的过程、中间环节、生物与社会机制、实验确认、机制假设、中介路径、解释而非相关。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a gearbox is opened, and the first gear turns the second until a rod at the far end moves.
core.cn: 核心意象：齿轮箱被剖开，第一枚齿轮带动第二枚，直到最远端的连杆动起来。

branches.en: THE WORKING PROCESS: the steps that carry the influence from start to finish.
branches.cn: 运作过程：把影响从头带到尾的那些步骤。

branches.en: THE TWO DOMAINS: molecular pathways in bodies and patterned action in societies.
branches.cn: 两个领域：身体内的分子通路与社会中的模式化行动。

branches.en: THE TESTED AND PROPOSED: a pathway confirmed by blocking, or merely put forward.
branches.cn: 已确认与已提出：经阻断确认的通路，或仅仅被提出。

branches.en: THE MEDIATED PATH: the route drawn through a middle variable.
branches.cn: 中介路径：穿过中间变量画出的路线。

branches.en: THE OPENED BOX: explanation that replaces a bare correlation.
branches.cn: 打开的箱子：取代单纯相关的解释。

intro.en: The phrase joins a Latin cause word to a Greek machine word carried into English through Latin and French.
intro.cn: 这个词组把拉丁语的「原因」与希腊语的「机械」（经拉丁语与法语进入英语）接起来。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies causa and machina; Greek mekhane stands behind the second half, and its deeper root is uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了「原因」与「机器」；后一半背后是希腊语「机械」，其更深词根不确定。

items.example: The first half of the phrase.
items.exampleCN: 这是词组的前一半。

items.example: It supplied the mechanism word.
items.exampleCN: 它提供了「机制」一词。

items.example: It carried the Greek word into European languages.
items.exampleCN: 它把希腊词带入欧洲各语言。

items.example: It marks mechanism as a system of parts.
items.exampleCN: 它把「机制」标为部件系统。

items.example: It forms mechanistic.
items.exampleCN: 它构成「机械式的」。

items.example: It forms mechanize.
items.exampleCN: 它构成「使机械化」。

items.example: The variable drawn in the middle of the path.
items.exampleCN: 指画在路径中间的那个变量。

items.example: The everyday word for a mechanism's shape.
items.exampleCN: 这是描述机制形态的日常词。

derivatives.zh: 希腊语「机械」经拉丁语与法语而来，义为「机制」
加形容词尾，义为「机械式的」
加动词尾，义为「使机械化」
加行为名词尾，义为「机械化」
同源名词，义为「机器」

definition_zh: 混淆变量；同时影响原因与结果、使观察到的关系失真的第三个变量
definition_en: a third variable that influences both the supposed cause and the effect, distorting the observed relationship
core_image: 两条本不相连的水管被同一只暗处的阀门同时控制，水一开两边都涨
scene: 调查发现喝咖啡的人成绩更好，但这些人往往睡得更少，研究者怀疑还有别的东西在同时起作用。Age is a confounding variable in the link between exercise and income.
sceneCN: 这里指同时影响两端的第三变量（第 1 个义项：同时影响原因与结果的变量）；句意为年龄是运动与收入之间关系中的混淆变量。

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语「倒在一起」而来的动词，义为「混淆；使困惑」
加已然词尾，义为「被混淆的；困惑的」
加行为名词尾，义为「混杂作用」
加施动者名词尾，义为「混杂因素」
由拉丁语「变化」而来的名词，义为「变量」

senses.title: A third variable affecting both ends
senses.titleCN: 同时影响两端的第三变量
senses.definition: a factor that influences both the proposed cause and the outcome, so that their link is partly its work
senses.definitionCN: 同时影响所设原因与结果、使其联系部分出自它的因素
senses.example: Temperature is a confounding variable in the study of ice cream and drowning.
senses.exampleCN: 在冰淇淋与溺水的研究中，气温是一个混淆变量。
senses.why: Confound means to pour together, and this variable pours two separate effects into one apparent link.
senses.whyCN: 「混淆」本义是倒在一起，这个变量把两种分开的效应倒进了一条看似存在的联系。

senses.title: An unmeasured confounder
senses.definition: a confounder that no one recorded, so its influence cannot be removed statistically
senses.definitionCN: 无人记录、因而无法在统计上剔除其影响的混杂因素
senses.example: The authors admit an unmeasured confounding variable may explain the result.
senses.exampleCN: 作者承认可能有未测量的混淆变量解释了这一结果。
senses.why: What is not in the dataset cannot be adjusted for, and that absence is the classic weakness of observation.
senses.whyCN: 不在数据集里的东西无法被校正，这种缺失正是观察研究的典型弱点。

senses.title: A variable that distorts an association
senses.definition: a factor that pushes an observed association away from the true causal effect
senses.definitionCN: 把观察到的关联推离真实因果效应的因素
senses.example: The apparent effect shrank once the confounding variable was included.
senses.exampleCN: 把该混淆变量纳入之后，表面上的效应缩小了。
senses.why: Distortion here is directional: the confounder adds or subtracts from the link rather than merely blurring it.
senses.whyCN: 这里的失真有方向：混淆变量对联系做加法或减法，而不只是把它弄模糊。

senses.title: A confounder removed by randomisation
senses.titleCN: 经随机化消除的混淆因素
senses.definition: a factor whose influence is balanced out because treatment is assigned by chance
senses.definitionCN: 因处理随机分配而被均衡掉的混杂因素
senses.example: Randomisation keeps every confounding variable balanced across groups.
senses.exampleCN: 随机化使每个混淆变量在组间保持均衡。
senses.why: Chance assignment does not identify the confounder; it makes the confounder equally present everywhere.
senses.whyCN: 随机分配并不识别混淆变量，而是让它在各处同等地存在。

senses.title: A confounding factor in field studies
senses.titleCN: 观察研究中的混杂因素
senses.definition: a factor that field researchers cannot hold constant and must therefore measure and adjust
senses.definitionCN: 现场研究者无法保持恒定、因而必须测量并校正的因素
senses.example: Field studies always carry confounding variables that the lab avoids.
senses.exampleCN: 现场研究总带着实验室能避开的混淆变量。
senses.why: The world does not hold variables still, so field work trades control for realism.
senses.whyCN: 世界不会把变量按住不动，因此现场研究以控制换取真实。

senses.title: A variable entangled with the predictor
senses.titleCN: 与预测变量纠缠的变量
senses.definition: a factor so closely tied to the supposed cause that the two cannot be separated without design
senses.definitionCN: 与所设原因关系紧密、不作设计便无法分开的因素
senses.example: Smoking is entangled with age, making age a confounding variable.
senses.exampleCN: 吸烟与年龄纠缠在一起，使年龄成为混淆变量。
senses.why: Entanglement is the statistical form of the pouring-together image, and separation requires design or adjustment.
senses.whyCN: 纠缠是「倒在一起」的统计形态，要分开就得靠设计或校正。

senses.title: A nuisance variable in an experiment
senses.definition: a factor that adds noise to an experiment and must be controlled though it is not of interest
senses.definitionCN: 给实验增添噪声、虽非研究焦点却必须控制的因素
senses.example: Room temperature acted as a confounding variable in the reaction times.
senses.exampleCN: 室温在反应时实验中充当了混淆变量。
senses.why: Not every confounder is dramatic; some simply add scatter and must still be handled.
senses.whyCN: 并非每个混淆变量都很戏剧化，有些只是增加离散，但仍须处理。

senses.title: A confounder behind a spurious link
senses.titleCN: 制造虚假联系的混杂因素
senses.definition: a factor that makes two unrelated things appear connected
senses.definitionCN: 使两件本无关系的事显得相连的因素
senses.example: The correlation vanished once the confounding variable was controlled.
senses.exampleCN: 控制该混淆变量后，相关性就消失了。
senses.why: Spurious links are the confounder's clearest signature, since removing it removes the appearance.
senses.whyCN: 虚假联系是混淆变量最清楚的签名，因为去掉它，表象也随之消失。

intro.en: Confounding variable joins a Latin verb meaning to pour together with a Latin adjective meaning changeable. The mixed influence of a third factor is poured into a link that belongs to two other things.
intro.cn: 这个词组把拉丁语中表示「倒在一起」的动词，与表示「可变」的形容词接在一起：第三个因素混合的影响被倒进了一条本属于另外两者的联系里。

items.en: Fundere meant to pour, and with the prefix for together it produced confundere, to pour together and hence to mix up.
items.cn: 这个词根意为「倒」，加上表示「共同」的前缀后构成「倒在一起」，因而指混淆。

items.en: The verb meant to mingle things so that they cannot be told apart, and English confound kept both the physical and the mental senses.
items.cn: 这个动词意为把事物混在一起以致无法分辨，英语的「混淆」保留了物理与心理两义。

items.en: English used confound for bringing to ruin and for confusing, and the statistical sense is much later.
items.cn: 英语中这个词先指使毁灭，也指使困惑，统计义要晚得多。

items.en: Variare meant to change or vary, from varius, diverse; English variable entered through French.
items.cn: 这个词根意为「变化」，来自表示「多样」的形容词；英语的「变量」经法语进入。

items.en: Epidemiology and statistics fixed confounding variable as the third factor that must be measured or balanced.
items.cn: 流行病学与统计学把「混淆变量」固定为必须测量或均衡的第三因素。

items.en: The shortened confounder is now common in research writing; its first record is uncertain.
items.cn: 缩短形式「混杂因素」如今在研究写作中很常见；其最早记录不确定。

note.en: The first group belongs to the confound family or looks similar; the second group names other roles a third variable can play.
note.cn: 第一组属于「混淆」同族或形近；第二组指第三变量可能扮演的其他角色。

entries.definition: To mix up or confuse, and in statistics to distort an association.
entries.definitionCN: 指弄混、使困惑，统计学中指使关联失真。

entries.definition: Mixed up, or used for an association distorted by a third factor.
entries.definitionCN: 指被弄混的，或指受第三因素干扰的关联。

entries.definition: The distortion itself, or the adjective for what causes confusion.
entries.definitionCN: 指失真本身，或形容造成混淆的。

entries.definition: The short noun for a confounding variable.
entries.definitionCN: 指混淆变量的简短名词形式。

entries.definition: To put together; it looks close but its root means to place, not to pour.
entries.definitionCN: 指组合；形近但词根意为「放置」，不是「倒」。

entries.definition: To keep within limits; its root is a boundary, not a pouring.
entries.definitionCN: 指限制在界限内；词根是「边界」，不是「倒」。

entries.definition: A variable through which the cause acts, part of the mechanism rather than a distortion.
entries.definitionCN: 指原因借以起作用的变量，属于机制而非干扰。

entries.definition: A variable that changes the strength of an effect, not its apparent existence.
entries.definitionCN: 指改变效应强弱的变量，而非改变效应是否存在。

entries.definition: A variable held constant by design, often to neutralise a confounder.
entries.definitionCN: 指设计中保持恒定的变量，常用来抵消混淆因素。

entries.definition: An unobserved factor that may distort a relationship, the informal name for a confounder.
entries.definitionCN: 指未被观察、可能使关系失真的因素，是混淆变量的通俗说法。

entries.definition: Any unwanted variable in a study, whether or not it confounds the link.
entries.definitionCN: 指研究中任何不想要的变量，未必真的混淆联系。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the hidden valve feeding two pipes, the unmeasured factor and the spurious link.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用同时供给两条水管的暗阀、未被测量的因素与虚假联系。

normal.en: To confound is to pour together, so a confounding variable pours its effect into someone else's link.
normal.cn: 混淆就是倒在一起，所以混淆变量把自己的效应倒进别人的联系里。

normal.en: The standard phrase is «control for confounding variables», the routine move in analysis.
normal.cn: 标准说法是「控制混淆变量」，是分析中的常规动作。

normal.en: Randomisation balances confounders without ever naming them.
normal.cn: 随机化在不点名的前提下均衡了混淆因素。

normal.en: A confounder differs from a mediator: one spoils the link, the other explains it.
normal.cn: 混淆变量不同于中介变量：前者破坏联系，后者解释联系。

normal.en: When a correlation vanishes after adjustment, a confounding variable was behind it.
normal.cn: 校正后相关消失，说明背后有混淆变量。

abstract.en: A confounder is a third person paying both sides of a conversation no one knows they are having.
abstract.cn: 混淆变量是第三个人，悄悄给一场无人自知正在进行的对话两边付钱。

abstract.en: The most dangerous confounder is the one nobody wrote down, because it cannot be subtracted.
abstract.cn: 最危险的混淆变量是无人记录的那一个，因为它无法被减去。

abstract.en: Randomisation is a way of making ignorance harmless by spreading it evenly.
abstract.cn: 随机化是通过把无知均匀铺开、使其无害的办法。

examples.en: Researchers adjusted for a confounding variable that had biased the earlier results.
examples.cn: 研究者对一个使早期结果产生偏差的混淆变量作了校正。

examples.en: An unmeasured confounding variable may explain the apparent effect.
examples.cn: 一个未测量的混淆变量也许能解释这一表面效应。

examples.en: Random assignment keeps confounding variables balanced between groups.
examples.cn: 随机分配使混淆变量在组间保持均衡。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「混淆」是把两样倒在一起，「变量」是会变的东西：会变的东西把两边的效应倒在一起，就是混淆变量

root: 「混淆」来自拉丁语 confundere「倒在一起」= con-「共同」+ fundere「倒」；「变量」来自拉丁语 variare「变化」，其形容词 varius 意为「多样的」。统计学与流行病学在二十世纪把这个词组固定为必须测量或均衡的第三因素；缩短形式「混杂因素」最早记录不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses run from the mechanism of distortion to its removal: a third factor affecting both ends, an unmeasured factor, a distorted association, a factor balanced by randomisation, a field-study problem, entanglement with the predictor, a nuisance variable, and the source of a spurious link.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从失真的机制延伸到消除：同时影响两端的因素、未测量因素、被失真的关联、经随机化均衡的因素、现场研究难题、与预测变量纠缠、干扰变量、虚假联系的来源。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two pipes that seem independent are both fed by one hidden valve, so both rise together.
core.cn: 核心意象：两条看似独立的水管都由同一只暗阀供水，于是一起上涨。

branches.en: THE MIXED INFLUENCE: a third factor that bends the observed link away from the truth.
branches.cn: 混合的影响：把观察到的联系掰离真相的第三因素。

branches.en: THE MISSING MEASUREMENT: the factor no one recorded, typical of field work.
branches.cn: 缺失的测量：无人记录的因素，是现场研究的典型问题。

branches.en: THE BALANCED FACTOR: the confounder made harmless by chance assignment.
branches.cn: 被均衡的因素：靠随机分配而变得无害的混淆因素。

branches.en: THE ENTANGLED AND NUISANCE: a factor tied to the predictor, or one that merely adds noise.
branches.cn: 纠缠与干扰：与预测变量绑在一起的因素，或只增加噪声的因素。

branches.en: THE SPURIOUS SIGNATURE: the appearance of a link that vanishes when the factor is removed.
branches.cn: 虚假的签名：去掉该因素后随之消失的联系假象。

intro.en: The phrase joins a Latin pouring verb to a Latin change word, and its picture is two influences mixed in one channel.
intro.cn: 这个词组把拉丁语的「倒」动词与「变化」词接起来，画面是两股影响混在同一通道里。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies confundere and variare; the statistical sense of the phrase is a twentieth-century development.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了「倒在一起」与「变化」；该词组的统计义是二十世纪的发展。

core_image: 一张试验田平面图，格子被分成不同处理区，中间留出对照行，播种顺序编成表
scene: 研究者先在纸上把试验田划分成若干区，标明哪些接受处理、哪些留作对照。Poor experimental design can make a real effect disappear.
sceneCN: 这里指实验的整体安排（第 1 个义项：处理与对照的总体规划）；句意为糟糕的实验设计会让真实效应消失。
